## Session 12d, follow-up: the release's selftest just after a pin move that changes the index version

22 November 2026 · branch `claude/s12d-release-selftest`, in S12d's session at the owner's word · [#157](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/157) · upstream `08e8bac8` (tag `1.0-release`), unchanged

The owner's first run of the release workflow failed in 26 seconds at its selftest, before the cut. It ran on `main` at `5668422`, #156's merge, to publish `:1.0-1861` ([run 45048774061](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/actions/runs/45048774061)), and stopped with "the selftest needs HEAD's first-parent line to reach another index version".

The selftest cuts against stubs over two commits of `main`'s first-parent line:
- p1, at least three back and at HEAD's index version, where it tags an app build's last release;
- p0, the newest commit at another index version.

Just after a pin move that changes the index version, HEAD is the only commit at its version, so no p1 exists. The release of the build the move brings was therefore refused until three more pull requests merged. The message named p0 alone, since the selftest had only run over a long history at one version.

**The fix,** in `scripts/release` alone: where no p1 exists, the selftest's own repository, which borrows this one's objects, merges three pull requests on HEAD.
- Each merge has HEAD's tree and is numbered past the newest pull request on HEAD's line.
- The commits carry a name of their own, since a runner has none.
- HEAD is then p1, and the sixteen cases cut the last of the three.

Where `main` holds three commits at HEAD's version, nothing changes, and `cut` itself is unchanged.

**Results,** on this Mac, with macOS's bash 3.2:
- `scripts/release selftest` passed every case:
  - at `main`'s `5668422` and at this branch's commit, by the new path;
  - at `ab5a051`, at index version 74, with this script, by the old path, with p1 `6acee4b` and p0 `2ea3f36` at 71.
- `scripts/release cut --dry-run --commit 5668422`, over the registry's and GitHub's answers, wrote nothing and refused nothing. It would publish the first release, `1.0-1861.1`:
  - the image `sha256:9ae7afd5…`, which `image.yml`'s run 45047338671 built and smoke-tested;
  - index version 75;
  - notes naming the 151 pull requests since the start.
- The release workflow's own selftest runs on Linux on this pull request.

**For the owner, once this merges:** run the release workflow on `main` again, first with dry run on, then off. It releases the build `edge` names once `image.yml` has smoke-tested this merge; to release #156's build itself, give `5668422` as its commit.

**Next:** as Session 12d's entry says.

**The server** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/PersonAnalytics.swift`, `CrossReferenceAnalytics.swift`, `KeptSeries.swift`; two members in `ServedIndex.swift` beside `people`, three lines in `Routes.swift` beside the graph's):

- **Kept:** each series is computed once per served index and kept (`KeptSeries`, an actor of at most 64 keys per kind, the least recently asked let go, a key asked while it is computed waiting for that computation, a failed one keeping nothing): `ServedIndex.personAnalytics` by years, scope and people, `ServedIndex.crossReferenceAnalytics` by the store's years and scope; a new index starts with none, as S24f's `ServedIndex.analytics` does.

## Session 24f, follow-up, upstream: the six kit issues, in three pull requests

22 November 2026 · branch `claude/interesting-bardeen-a9dd63` · [#155](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/155) · upstream `f011ab04`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1967](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1967), [#1968](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1968) and [#1969](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1969), open

This entry covers the six issues this repository filed upstream on 14 and 15 November: #1907, #1911 to #1913, #1927 and #1928.
- The app's plan of record (decision 138) makes them web-authored pull requests, merging after 1.0 (1861)'s upload, which is done.
- This session ran at the orchestrator's word of 21 November. No PLAN row names it.
- Three of the six follow S24f's workarounds.

Each pull request is cut from `v2` at `21c77370`, is labelled `Mac`, asks for Mac verification as its own Mac check, and is not merged. Under rule 4 they change shared files, and this repository changes only its records.

**FRUS-Explorer#1967, Mac check 32 (#1907, #1927): Related Documents' and Chronology's rows read a reader's summaries from the store a host names.**
- `RelatedDocumentsEngine.rank(…)` and `IndexingPipeline.documentsInDateRange(…)` each take `userSource: SearchUserSource = .index`, as #1902's `documentSnippets(forKeys:maxLength:userSource:)` does.
- From the index, the default and the app's call, each runs the statement it ran before, by text and binds. Two pins, taken with the statement trace on `v2`'s code, hold them.
- With a store, Chronology's statement gathers the user's summaries in one scan of `user_search` and joins them after the index's two tables, so the rows and their order are the index's.

**FRUS-Explorer#1968, Mac check 33 (#1912, #1913, #1928): three of S24f's workarounds can go once a pin move carries it.**
- `ChronologyGrouping.group(…)` and `makeChart(fromCounts:…)` take the locale their labels are written in. The server can pass `SearchItem.locale` and drop `ChronologyLabels`.
- `CorpusAnalyticsService`'s occurrence series has a cache of its own. `ServedIndex` can drop its second service, `occurrences`.

## Session 24f: Corpus Analytics and Chronology

14 November 2026 · branch `claude/epic-taussig-98f970` · [#150](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/150) · upstream `f011ab04`, unchanged

Phase 3's row S24f, the features track's wave 7: Corpus Analytics and Chronology, over the kit S24a's FRUS-Explorer#1896 and S24b's #1899 moved, and #1906's `CountCopy` and `ScopeFacets`. The branch was cut from `main` at `13ee15d`, #145's merge, and kept in local commits until the push. No upstream pull request, no pin move, no migration, no `Package.swift` or lockfile change.

**The server** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/CorpusAnalytics.swift`, `Chronology.swift`, two lines in `Routes.swift` beside the graph's):
- **`GET /api/v1/analytics/corpus`** gives a term's chart as the app's `AnalyticsView` draws it for one committed term: every series the kit's `CorpusAnalyticsService` over the served index, fetched in `reloadData()`'s order (the totals, the per-volume breakdown, the occurrence availability, the occurrences when the reader asked for them and the term can be so counted, the six axes' series); the folding by volume (`AnalyticsSourceColoring`) at the colours asked (6 to 12, 8 by default), the shares, the fit line, the footnotes, the empty states, and the table, the kit's `AnalyticsChartTables.corpusSeriesTable`. Its parameters: the term, the axis, the measure, the values, the years (1776 to the corpus's last year), the colours, and a scope, which the server resolves as the scope bar's item seeds it (a subseries's indexed volumes, a volume, a detected topic's indexed volumes through `ScopeFacets`, or a scope's volumes and name), refusing one that holds no indexed volume, which the app's menu disables, rather than reading it as the whole corpus.
- **`…/corpus/documents`** gives Search's count of the documents the hand-off link opens and the dispersion beside it (`AnalyticsSearchHandoff.match`, `CorpusDispersion`), over the served index's search; none for an `=` word the chart refuses. **`…/corpus/export`** gives the CSV: the kit's table headed by the kit's method block (`provenancedCSV(_:for:)`), for a host of the server's own (its name and version, US English, Gregorian, the browser's time zone), named by the app's `filenameStem`. **`…/corpus/plate`** gives a figure's caption band, the kit's `plateLines(for:)`, and its file's name.
- **`GET /api/v1/analytics/context`** gives what both screens open on: the corpus's years (`ManifestStore.corpusDateRange`, mirrored), Chronology's first range (`seedDefaultsAndApply`), the administration presets (`AdministrationPresetMenu.presets`, mirrored over the kit's `AdministrationProfile`, the bundled `administration-profiles-index.json` decoded once by the kit's loader, beside the other files in `ServerResources`), the colours' counts, and the scope menu's corpus-wide items: the indexed subseries and their volumes, and By Detected Topic, each narrowing category's sub-categories with their indexed counts, over `documents?.subjectsByVolume ?? profiles.resolvedByVolume`, as the app's scope bars read them.
- **`GET /api/v1/chronology`** gives a range's documents as the app's view model's `reload()` loads them, every rule the kit's `ChronologyGrouping` over the pipeline's `documentsInDateRange` and `dateBucketVolumeCounts`, with the view's legend filter, summary, chips, span and direction labels and aggregate lines; **`…/chronology/export`** and **`…/plate`** its chart's CSV and caption band, the web's own, since the app's Chronology exports nothing.
- **The served stack** keeps one `CorpusAnalyticsService` per index, whose caches end with it as the app's `invalidateCache()` empties them, and a second for the occurrence series alone: the kit caches those under "occ:" and the term, which a document term so spelt would meet in one shared service, one user's request then answering another's (FRUS-Explorer#1913).

**What is mirrored, and held** (`AnalyticsMirrorParityTests`): what the views decide between the kit and the screen, under their names, line beside line with the app's source: the year filters and `yearRangeIsCustom`, the measure's and the normalisation's gates, `normalizedValue`, the occurrences' decades, the headings, the export's title, table, period column and statement, the footnotes, the hand-off's words and the dispersion line, the scope bar's items, the presets, the corpus's years, the export's name, the palette's counts; Chronology's `reload()`, legend filter, summary, span and direction labels and `ChronologyAggregateText`; and every word the server or `copy.ts` takes, under the app's key. The browser's view is the chart and its table at once, so the view's mode is the chart's (`isNormalized` reads it).

**Two choices, each said in the code and SPEC:**
- **Chronology's labels in US English.** The kit writes a section's and a bar's label in the process's locale, which in the Linux container is World English (`en_001`), "3 February 1969"; the app on the owner's devices writes "February 3, 1969", and the web's dates are US English. So the server writes the label again from its bucket by the kit's three formats in `en_US` (`ChronologyLabels`), held to the kit's source; an upstream change giving `ChronologyGrouping`'s labels a locale, FRUS-Explorer#1912, would retire it.
- **The CSV's scope line follows the chip.** The view passes its `scopeLabel` to the statement, which a hand-off may leave nil beside its volumes, and the CSV would then call a scoped chart the whole corpus; the server passes the chip's name, Selected volumes.

**The browser app** (`web/src/analytics/`, `api/analytics.ts`; lines in `router.tsx`, `AppShell.tsx`, `copy.ts` and `app.css` beside their kin): `/analytics/corpus` and `/chronology`, opened from the header's Analytics menu, the Mac's, Chronology after a divider. Each chart is drawn by Vega-Lite from the server's series, with its table beside it, the CSV from the server, and the figure, PNG or SVG, drawn in the browser with the kit's caption band. Vega runs as its expression interpreter (`ast`) and adds no style sheet or menu, so it draws under the app's policy, which runs no evaluated script and applies no inline style sheet; Vega and Vega-Lite load with the analytics pages alone (a chunk of 853 kB). The measure, values and colours are kept in the browser under the app's own keys. SPEC's Corpus Analytics and Chronology say the rest, and what is not here: comparing terms, saved and recent queries, the scrub across the chart, a figure's PDF (S25a's Gotenberg can give it from the SVG), Chronology's hover magnifier and its word cloud for the range (S24i).

**The done-when, shown:**

- **Subjects**, after Mentions and Active: the kit's `PersonSubjectAffinity.rank(mentionCounts:topSubjectsByVolume:limit:)` of the person's `volumeMentionCounts(forRollupId:)` over the bundled volume profiles' `topSubjects(forVolumeId:)`, the producer the ranking's sum needs, never the document subject index, whose scores are a corpus IDF (`ResolvedSubject.score`'s doc comment), with the app's limit, 8; none without the profiles or a mention, or when the store cannot count them, as the app's `try?` shows none. **The decisions:**
- **The pivot is a route of its own,** by the subject's ref, not part of the sheet's answer: a subject's volumes reach 547, and a sheet would carry every chip's list unopened. It reads the bundled files alone, so it answers whatever the served index holds, as the app's sheet lists volumes not downloaded; a ref neither file names has no volumes, the app's empty sheet.
- **Its two doors wait:** the app's pivot also offers "Archival profile of these volumes", Archival Analytics over them (S24h's surface), and "Browse this topic in the index", the Topic Index, which no row has built; SPEC says so.
- **The description's chip too:** the app badges each of the header's claims so that a reader tells the volumes' words from the register's; the register's chip without the description's would leave half of that.
- **A post is known by its place,** not the kit's `id`, which the register gives twice in one career (`taylor-francis-xavier`'s two posts as Ambassador at Large, one with an end and one without); the app's `ForEach(career.a)` meets the same pair.

## Session 21g: corrections on the web, and the People screen

14 November 2026 · branch `claude/heuristic-pascal-dd9ccc` · upstream `6b6932aa`, then `b124a59b` with `main` (#140)

Phase 3's round 7 on the server track, the S21 group's fifth and last row on the web and the server track's last, after S21f, beside S24f's features row, the timing flakes' follow-up and the pin move to `b124a59b`, on PLAN's defaults, migration 8. A curator corrects the index everyone shares in its two ways, rule 7's two writes: a document's classification in the Research rail, and the person rollup's identities on the People screen, which phase 1 left; each is kept and logged, applied at once on a Standalone server and at the next export an Import server installs. SPEC's new section, Operating modes ▸ Corrections on the web and the People screen, is the whole account; this entry says what was built where, the decisions, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and the group's shared records. The branch was cut from `main` at `48dbc22`, #139's merge, and the work was kept in local commits until the push; `main` was merged once, at `84666ee`, since #140 changed README's Status line too, which brought #140's pin move to `b124a59b` (#1904, access alone) and #141's fixes of two timing flakes into the final runs. No file of the app changed.

**The kit, surveyed first.** Everything the row's done-when calls is public at `6b6932aa`: `applyClassificationOverrides(_:volumeId:)`, `consolidatePersonRollup(overrides:forceReload:)` (S21a's #1870), `consolidatePersonRollupIfNeeded` and `runPostIndexPasses(overrides:)`, `PersonClusterOverrideData` and `DocumentClassificationOverrideData`, `PersonMentionStore`'s list, members, candidates and `representativeMember(forRollupId:)`, `PersonEntry`'s `eraText` and `roleEraSubtitle`, `FRUSDocumentAST.isShapedAsEditorialNote` and `applyingClassificationOverride`, and `PersonAuthorityIndex` with its entries' role, years and links. Two sections of the app's person sheet read members internal at the pin, which the orchestrator was told before anything was written around them: the register's career, `POCOMIndex.career(forSlug:)` with `POCOMCareer` and `POCOMAssignment`'s `titleText`, `dateRangeText` and `nt`, which also fill a life year the name authority lacks (`PersonLifespan.years(authority:career:)`); and the subjects, `VolumeSubjectProfiles.topSubjects(forVolumeId:)` and `ResolvedSubject`, which the app's `PersonSubjectAffinity` ranks over. They wait, below.

**The store** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserCorrections.swift`, `UserStoreMigrations.swift`, `PostgreSQLMigrations.swift`):
- Migration 8, in both dialects, makes `correction_log`: one entry for each correction made or undone, `correction` (`classification` or `person`), `action` (`made` or `undone`), the override row it names, the classification's document with its value and what the TEI said, or the person correction's kind and the records it anchors on, `user_id`, `made_at` and `applied_at`, empty while the index has not taken it; the PostgreSQL store's carries `rowid`, the order the log is read in, which SQLite keeps for every table.
- `CorrectionLogStore`, written once on `RelationalUserStore` in SQL both stores read: a merge kept once either way round and never of a record with itself, a separation once, each undone by its id, as the app's `PersonClusterOverrideStore` keeps them; a classification kept one per document by `CorrectionStore.record`'s rule, now a helper the two share, and its restore, which removes the document's every row and logs the value it puts back; each with its log entry in the same transaction, none moving the search mark. The log is read newest first, a document's entries, every person entry, the entries waiting, and the standing restores, a document whose latest entry is a restore and which holds no correction now.

**The index** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexCorrections.swift`, `LibraryIndexing.swift`, `IndexUpkeep.swift`, `IndexImport.swift`, `Readiness.swift`, `JobQueue.swift`):
- `IndexCorrections.apply(to:restoring:rebuildingRollup:)`, the app's sequence over the kit's calls: each restore through the volume-scoped entry point, which keeps nothing for the replay, as `DocumentClassificationOverrideStore.saveAndApply` restores one, its value the TEI's parse read again, else the one logged; then every classification, oldest first, which the pipeline keeps for `indexVolume`'s replay; then, when asked, `consolidatePersonRollup(overrides:forceReload: false)` with every person correction, newest first, as the app's `saveAndReconsolidate` calls it.
- A Standalone server's one writer: the job `indexCorrections`, which a correction made while one waits joins, applies the entries waiting through `withWriter(holding: nil)`, so that search answers meanwhile, marks them applied, and the served stack is opened again; a start queues one for what a stop left waiting (`resumeCorrectionsAtStart`). Every other writer keeps them: `openWriter()` gives the index every classification again, the passes after indexing take every person correction (`postIndexPasses`, at the indexing's, the removal's, the whole pass's and the start's four calls), and the kit's pass over every volume, which replays none, is followed by the set again. A store that cannot say what the corrections are fails the writer's opening, and the passes wait, so that no rollup is rebuilt without them.
- An import's step, `applying_corrections` (`IndexCorrectionReplay`), in both modes, after the copy is checked and stripped and before its integrity check: the kit's read-write pipeline over the copy gives it every classification, every standing restore and, when the store keeps a person correction, the rollup built again with them; the copy's log is then folded into it and its journal a rollback journal's again, for Import mode's immutable open; and once the copy is installed, the entries waiting when the step read them are applied. A store with no correction leaves the step out, so an import's steps are as before.

**The routes** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/People.swift`, `Corrections.swift`, with one line each in `Routes.swift`, `UserData.swift`, `AdminBackup.swift`, `ServedIndex.swift` and `ServerResources.swift`):
- `GET /api/v1/people`, the kit's `allPersonsSortedByName()` by the app's sections, each row's line the app's subtitle, with `version`, a digest of the list, read once for each served stack (`ServedIndex.people`); `GET /api/v1/people/{rollupId}`, the sheet, the bundled name authority decoded once for the register's years and role and the Wikidata link.
- Under `/api/v1/me`'s guard, each write refused without the curator role: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE …/documents/{d}/classification`; `POST people/merges` and `people/separations`, against the `version` the page was given, the merge's anchors each identity's representative record, as the app's `mergeRollup` takes them; `GET people/corrections` and `DELETE people/corrections/{id}`. Each answers `applied`, once a Standalone server's job has applied it within half a minute, `waiting`, or `nextExport` on an Import server. An admin's `GET /api/v1/admin/corrections` reads the log, each entry named from the served index, which Administration ▸ Corrections shows.
- A curator's import of the Mac's research that brings corrections queues the job, giving every correction again, on a Standalone server with an index (`Imports.swift`).
- The rules the views apply, the app's, mirrored as `PeopleRules` (the row's subtitle, the sections, the life years, the register's role, Mentions); the parse a restore reads, the reader's.

**The browser app** (`web/src/people/`, `web/src/research/ClassificationSection.tsx`, `web/src/api/people.ts`, lines beside their kin in `router.tsx`, `BrowseAxes.tsx`, `ResearchRail.tsx`, `ReaderScreen.tsx`, `copy.ts`, `api/types.ts` and `app.css`): People, one of Browse's axes, with its search field, its letters, each row one stop with the app's spoken line, the editors' annotations' caption of the volumes that tag their people, the sheet, and for a curator Corrections, Merge with another person… with its picker and question, each suggestion's Merge and each record's Separate; the screen says what a correction did, and a curator on an Import server that the next export is given it. Administration ▸ Corrections (`web/src/admin/CorrectionsPane.tsx`), after Library, lists the log.

**The decisions:**
- **Import mode: kept, and given to the next export,** PLAN's default for the open question, which the owner has not answered; the alternative opened the served export writable. Three things follow, each in SPEC: the step runs in the import's job, so rule 7's immutable open is kept; a restore of a document the Mac itself corrected stands at every install, read again from the TEI, since the Mac's export carries its correction again each time; and the rollup is built again only when the store keeps a person correction, from the store's set, so the Mac's merges and separations reach it through a curator's import of the Mac's research, which INSTALL says.

- **A request waits for its job,** half a minute at most, as the app's sheet waits for its consolidation before it closes; behind a long job it answers that the correction waits.
- **The log has a pane of Administration's, Corrections,** the web's own, after Library: each entry's time, curator, what it did, by the document's head or the records' names from the served index, and whether the index holds it; a backup carries it with the store.

## Session 24e, follow-up, upstream: the kit's stamp tests, each over a store of its own

13 November 2026 · branch `claude/kit-test-race-records-1efabb` · [#135](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/135) · upstream `39859a51`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1903](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1903), open

**Since merged** (the pin move to `6b6932aa` records it): the owner merged FRUS-Explorer#1903 on 14 November (02:01 UTC) as `6b6932aa`, after Mac check 28. Its tree is its head's, `ffc3fc32`, and it went onto `v2` at `39859a51`, the branch's base. A pin move of its own took it, to `6b6932aa`, with nothing to follow, as this entry predicted: `FRUSCoreKitTests` runs its 2,509 tests there with no skip, and the golden files stand (the entry above, "Session 24e, second follow-up").

A race in the kit's tests, which the daily watch met at the pin, fixed upstream by the owner's word of 13 November; no PLAN row names it. The watch's run that day ([43444877747](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/actions/runs/43444877747), at `39859a51`, reported in [#106](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/issues/106)) failed `FRUSCoreKitTests` on one test, `DateIndexingAccuracyTests`' "needsDateReindex — returns true before markDateReindexComplete is called", which this repository's CI had passed at the same commit (run 43439295815). The CI runs the kit's suites at the pin, so the race could turn `main` red too. The pull request is `claude/kit-test-race-date-reindex`, cut from `v2` at `39859a51`, which `v2` still is. It is labelled `Mac`, asks for Mac verification as Mac check 28, and is not merged. Under rule 4 it changes shared files, the kit's test folder alone, and this repository changes only its records.

**The race.** Every test pipeline built without a stamp store of its own shares one: `testIndexingStamps` in the package, `UserDefaults.standard` in Xcode. The failing test removed the date-index stamp from it, built a pipeline and read the stamp, while `needsDateReindexFalse`, which Swift Testing runs beside it, marked the same key and removed it after. The FTS stamp test and the rollup gate's fingerprint test cleared and read stamps in the same store. The first never failed, since no other test writes its key, and the second was safe only through fixture ids unique to it.

**The fix,** test files only: `makeTestPipeline` builds a pipeline over a store of the test's own when given a suite name. `makeIsolatedStamps(_:)` makes it: the kit's `InMemoryIndexingStampStore` in the package, a `UserDefaults` suite in Xcode, whose app initialiser takes one. The four tests take one, and `testStamps`, the accessor they cleared the shared store through, goes. No test's result now depends on a stamp in the shared store, and nothing needed `.serialized`. One cold review found no defect, and two comments that said too much, now fixed.

**Measured** (the pull request has the figures, each against `v2` run the same way):
- **Linux,** over `main` at `fedd7cd` in `swift:6.4-noble`:
  - `DateIndexingAccuracyTests` run alone 100 times failed 5 times at `v2`, each at the watch's line, and never at the branch.
  - A repro suite, never committed, calls the real tests: the pair together 300 times in one process, two copies of the FTS test 100 times, and two of the fingerprint test 50 times. It had 1 to 2, 0 and 24 to 40 issues a run at `v2`, and none at the branch in three runs.
  - The whole run: 4,156 tests at both heads, every target passing, with the one named skip. `FRUSCoreKitTests` ran 2,509 tests, and three more runs of it at each head all passed.
  - Over the new `main`, `3f8cd6a` (S23e's #134), whose own CI passed at `v2`, the branch's tree passed every target but two of the web server's PostgreSQL tests. Those failed on "too many clients already", a known failure under load, and passed when `FRUSLightServerTests` ran alone (359 tests).
- **Xcode,** on an iPhone 17e (iOS 27.2):
  - The repro had 153 to 170, 101 to 108 and 1 to 3 issues a run at `v2`, and none at the branch.
  - The three changed suites, 47 tests, passed ten repetitions at both heads.
  - The rest of Mac check 28 gives `v2`'s figures at the branch: both builds with `v2`'s warning lines, the unit target's 7,999 tests with `v2`'s one failure and skips, `swift test`'s 4,490, and the Mac app's symbols identical.
  - In Xcode the host app writes the shared store too. After the branch's runs it held the date-index, FTS and broken-references stamps, which no test there writes.

**For the next pin move, which carries it:** nothing to follow.
- No kit source changes, so no `Package.swift`, CI allow-list or `Compatibility.swift` change.
- `FRUSCoreKitTests` keeps 2,509 tests and gains no skip.
- The golden files' source digest (`UpstreamDigest.directories`) covers no test folder. The parity suite passed over `main` with the branch's tree, and this pull request alone stales no golden file.

`kit-test-race-handover.md`, in the orchestrator's notes folder, has the rest.

**Left, named in the pull request:** `CitationStyleTests`, Xcode's alone, and the app's `SettingsSyncCoordinatorTests` clear and set `SettingsKeys.citationStyle` in `UserDefaults.standard`, beside each other. It is the same kind of race on another store. It needs an app change, since `CitationStyle.current` reads `.standard` itself.

## Session 22e, follow-up, upstream: the Zotero client's waits on Zotero's word, bounded

14 November 2026 · branch `claude/wizardly-sutherland-287ad1` · [#149](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/149) · upstream `f011ab04`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1916](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1916), open

This fixes a finding of S22e's cold reviews, upstream, at the orchestrator's word of 14 November. No PLAN row names it.
- The kit's `ZoteroAPIClient`, which the server's Send to Zotero Library calls (`ZoteroSend.swift`), made `UInt64(seconds * 1_000_000_000)` of a 429's `Retry-After` and of an advisory `Backoff`.
- `UInt64(_:)` traps on a negative, NaN, infinite or huge value. On a server a trap ends the process, and every request in flight with it. A well-formed but long value held the request for as long as it said.
- The pull request is `claude/zotero-retry-wait-bound`, cut from `v2` at `f011ab04`, which `v2` still is. It is labelled `Mac`, asks for Mac verification as Mac check 31, and is not merged.
- Under rule 4 it changes shared files, the kit's Zotero client and its suite, and this repository changes only its records.

**The waits.** In every kit, only the Zotero client's two waits read a value from outside: the `Backoff` after a successful write, and a 429's `Retry-After` before each of up to three retries. The NARA client throws `rateLimited` at once on a 429 and never waits. The generator cores' waits and the app's are their own constants.

**The bound.** It was proposed to the orchestrator before it was written, and approved with three additions: the trade-off below in the pull request, the lower edge pinned, and the web's held request named here.
- **Reading:** a header counts only when its seconds are finite and not negative. "nan", "inf", "-1" and the like count as absent, as an HTTP date already did, so a 429 waits the 30 s default. "-0" reads as 0, a choice that the tests pin.
- **The cap:** 60 s for any one wait. A `Retry-After` past it reaches the caller at once as `rateLimited`, carrying Zotero's seconds, with no retry: Zotero's rule is to wait at least that long. A `Backoff` past it is waited for 60 s and the send goes on, a bounded departure from Zotero's advice, since the write it came with succeeded.
- **Unchanged:** values up to a minute, the three retries, the 30 s default, and the public API. The waits go through a sleep that a test can replace, an internal initialiser.
- **The trade-off,** for the owner to weigh at the check: a 429 past a minute on a write after a send's first now stops the send there, as an exhausted retry already does. The writes before it stay in Zotero with no history row, so a second send duplicates them. A send that records how far it got, or resumes, is named as a possible follow-up.

**Measured** (the pull request has the figures, each against `v2` run the same way):
- **Linux,** over `main` in `swift:6.4-noble`:
  - At `13ee15d`, `v2` ran 4,230 tests and the branch 4,243. Every test passed but, at the branch, the golden files' 22 freshness issues, which come from the source digest.
  - Over `db0cba7`, with the golden files' recorded digest set to the branch's, all 4,251 passed, so the branch changes nothing those files hold.
  - The kit's Zotero suites alone passed 20 runs.
- **Xcode,** on an iPhone 17 (iOS 27.2):
  - both builds had `v2`'s warning lines;
  - the unit target ran 8,012 tests (`v2` 7,999), with `v2`'s one failure and the same skips;
  - `swift test` ran 4,512 (`v2` 4,499);
  - the Mac app lost 4 symbols and gained 22, each the change's own.
- **On `v2`'s client,** a suite never committed, through the public API, trapped on a `Backoff` of "nan", "-1" or "inf" and on a `Retry-After` of "1e300", on Linux and in the simulator. It slept on "3600" until the one-minute limit. At the branch each passed at once.

**One cold review** found no correctness bug, and ran mutations that the suite catches. It did find gaps, now fixed:
- The public client's real sleep was untested, so a no-op sleep passed. A test now holds it to two waits of 0.1 s.
- The `Backoff` doc comment claimed Zotero's "consistency" allowance for the send's remaining writes. It now calls them a bounded departure.
- A public doc comment named an internal member.
- `pause` relied on its callers, and now clamps.

**For the next pin move, which carries it:** nothing to follow in the code.
- No public API changes, so nothing in `Sources/` does. `ZoteroSend.swift` maps `.rateLimited` to its 503 without reading the seconds.
- No `Package.swift`, CI allow-list or `Compatibility.swift` change, no new skip, and the index version is unchanged.
- `FRUSCoreKitTests` gains the suite's 13 tests.
- FRUSCoreKit is in the golden files' source digest, so `make-golden` remakes them: a run over `main` with their recorded digest set to the branch's passed whole, so only their provenance, and the index summary's timings, should move. Nothing on the indexing path changes, so the build-1812 export serves if the owner chooses it.

`zotero-retry-handover.md`, in the orchestrator's notes folder, has the rest.

**A possible web follow-up, not opened:** the send runs inside its HTTP request, so it can outlast a reverse proxy's read timeout. nginx's default is 60 s, which INSTALL's recipes keep.
- This is true at the pin too: three 30 s waits for a 429 with no `Retry-After` take 90 s.
- After the bound, one write waits at most 3 × 60 + 60 = 240 s.
- When the proxy gives up, the browser sees a 504 while the send goes on, and a second send duplicates the items.
- Running the send as a job the browser polls, or stopping it when the client disconnects, would close this.

**Next:** the owner's Mac check 31 and merge of FRUS-Explorer#1916; the next pin move carries it.

## Session 22e, follow-up: the cold review's ten findings on S22e's code, verified

14 November 2026 · branch `claude/busy-neumann-dfd31a` · [#148](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/148) · upstream `f011ab04`

A session with no row of its own, after S22e. The cold review run for the pin move to `f011ab04` (#146) diffed against a stale local `main`, so it read S22e's merged code (#144) and left ten findings that nobody had verified. Each was verified against `main` at `13ee15d`: seven hold, in whole or in part, and are fixed, each with a test, which but for the duplication's fails on the code before it; three do not, for the reasons below. A mutation run undid each fix in turn, and each time its own tests failed and no others. Keys: stubs alone, the owner's word of 14 November; no real key is anywhere. No upstream pull request, no pin move, no migration.

**The verdicts,** in the review's order (lines at `b3ecb37`):
1. **NARA's answers shared across users: holds.** `NARAAnswerCache` kept an answer by its query alone, so `cached` told a user that someone had run the same search that day. Dropping the flag would not have closed it: a cached answer also came sooner, and with the instance's key it left `GET /api/v1/nara`'s count where it was. An answer is now kept for the user who asked, by their id and the search (`NARARoutes.Call.cacheKey(for:)`), so another user's same search asks NARA itself and is counted. The key's parts are each written after their length, where a field holding the separator, U+001F, could make two searches share one. `eachUsersAnswersAreTheirOwn`, two users behind the proxy. A user is who the server says: with `FRUS_AUTH=none` every visitor is the one user, and shares its answers as it shares its 100 calls, which SPEC and INSTALL now say, so a server that others reach keeps their searches apart only by signing them in; keeping none there would spend the shared 100 on every visit to the same document's Sources.
2. **The quota counted only the calls NARA answered: holds.** The kit's client tells `recordNARACatalogAPICall()` of a call only after a 2xx (`NARACatalogClient.executeSearch`). So a 403, 429 or 5xx, or a call NARA never answered, was counted nothing, and a user whose searches failed could ask without end with the instance's key. A call is now counted as it is made: the kit's client asks its provider for the key before each call, as `NARACatalogKeyProvider`'s contract says, and the server's provider counts there, the kit unchanged. Each search's hold is its own (`NARAQuota.Hold`): a call made is counted and held no longer, and what the search held and did not make is let go when it ends. `aCallNARARefusesOrNeverAnswersIsCountedToo`: 500, 403 and no answer at all, each counted, and a lot's search refused at its first spelling counted one.
3. **Identical searches at once each called NARA: holds.** All missed the cache, each held the quota, and each asked NARA. A search under way is now joined: `NARAAnswerCache.answer(to:now:search:)` keeps a task by the same key, the search's own, not the request's, so a request cancelled does not stop it for the others, and an answer with records is kept when it ends. `aSearchAskedAgainWhileItRunsWaitsForIt`: four at once with the instance's key, on a quota of one call, the stand-in holding NARA's answer until three have joined; NARA is asked once, all four are answered, and one call is counted. Before, three of the four were refused `NARA_QUOTA_REACHED`.
4. **The NARA Catalog section empty with a key and no query: holds, as a divergence the server cannot yet reach.** The app's `naraResultSection` falls through to "No matching record found in the NARA Catalog." and its manual search when it has no results, no search and no error; the web's drew nothing. Every NARA panel the server writes carries a search today, since `catalogPanel` is called only for the three parse cases `catalogSearch()` answers. The component now falls through as the app's does. It asks whether the search runs, never `isPending` alone, since a query that never runs stays pending. `SourcesScreen.test.tsx`.
5. **The frame took ⇧⌘H with no user data: holds.** S22e's review left the chord to the browser in the parent page on a server that keeps no user data. The frame's host script still took it over any selection in the text, and posted a shortcut the parent dropped. The parent now tells the frame as each page loads whether the chord is the app's (`{kind: 'highlightKey', on}`), once the server has said whether it keeps user data, and the host leaves it to the browser when it is not; until then the frame keeps it, as it did. `ReaderScreen.test.tsx` holds the parent's half. `highlights-keyboard.spec.ts` holds both on Chromium: the page is told by a routed `/api/v1/me` that the server keeps none, and the chord reaches the frame's window untaken, with nothing made.
6. **The `CancellationError` arm dead, a disconnect answered as 502: does not hold as stated.** The NARA arm was dead: the kit's client gives every failure of a call as `networkError`, a cancelled one too, and nothing in a search throws `CancellationError` itself. The Zotero arm is live, since the kit's `send` throws it between its batches and from its back-off's wait. But no client's going is answered or logged as 502. This server cancels a route's work when its client goes only inside `whileClientConnected`, which neither route's outside calls use, and `ProblemMiddleware` logs no `APIProblem`. A search whose client has gone runs to its end, its answer kept and its calls counted, as the cache and the quota want. The dead arm is gone, and both places say why.
7. **Look Up's route outside the guard and every limit: holds in part.** It needs no session, origin check or token. Like Citation Lookup's routes, it reads the corpus, the bundled indexes and the request's own text, keeps nothing, asks nothing outside and acts for no user, and the corpus answers anyone (SPEC, Local accounts). Its body must be JSON, which a page elsewhere cannot send without a preflight the server never grants. Its cost, measured in the build image over the fixture volume: the analyzer reads the worst selection, 20,000 characters of distinct lot numbers, in 58–70 ms (1,394 candidates), and 20,000 of prose in 8 ms. A page already parsed costs under a millisecond. What held: `start` and `end` were not held to the selection's limit, so a request of one character, `end` at `Int.max`, read the whole document's text as its passage, d93's 35,309 units, 0.11 s with its first parse. The span is now read over the selection's 20,000 at most, with the app's passage around it. `lookUpsPassageIsHeldToTheSelectionsLimit`. No per-client limit was added: the server has none on its corpus routes, which cost as much or more (a Citation Lookup batch of 500 citations), and the analyzer's work is now bounded by the request alone.
8. **Export not held while the Zotero row works: holds.** The app's sheet holds Export, the RIS file and the send on one `isExporting`, and its Export clears a failed send's error and its Save a Zotero file instead as it starts (`runExport()`). The web's held the row while Export ran, but not Export while the row sent or saved its file, and both wrote the sheet's lines. Export now waits for the row, and the row, held, lets a failed send's error and its way on go. `CollectionExport.test.tsx`, with the send held open, and with Export held open after a failed send.
9. **The mirror's base URL a process-wide static: does not hold.** True as a description, with no effect. A server reads `FRUS_SERVICES_MIRROR` once, at its start, as it reads the environment. The protocol answers only in the sessions of a server whose configuration names the mirror (`OutsideServices.session(mirrored:)`), so a server without one never asks it, whatever the static holds. Only the tests make two servers in one process, and one test names a mirror.
10. **The duplicated checks: holds, as duplication.** The server's three `KEY_UNREADABLE` blocks, the user's NARA key, the instance's and the user's Zotero key, are one helper, `OutsideServices.storedKey(_:of:in:unreadable:)`, each with its own sentence. No test had covered them: `aStoredKeyTheKeyFileCannotOpenSaysWhose` seals each under another key file, and guards the change, passing before it as after. The browser's two Zotero key checks are `holdsZoteroKey`.

**The cold reviews,** one of the server and the keys, one of the browser app and the specs, each given the diff against `origin/main` and none of this session's reasoning. What held was changed: Export left a failed send's Save a Zotero file instead to run beside it (now cleared as Export starts, above); the frame was told the chord was not the app's while `/api/v1/me` was pending, on a server that keeps user data too (now told nothing until the answer); the cache's visitors under `FRUS_AUTH=none` (the records now say so); the spec pressed the chord without waiting for the frame's load, which tells it (now waits for it); and a test's count, which the full run had already met. Left as they are: a search that joins one under way takes its refusal, in the words of the key that search used, which differs only when the same user changed their key between two identical searches running at once. Found beside the diff and left for a follow-up: the proxy's table of the users it has resolved (`ProxyHeaderResolver.known.users`, `UserData.swift`) is keyed by Swift `String`, whose equality is canonical equivalence, while the store compares bytes, so two names a proxy sends in different normal forms, `José` composed and decomposed, are two users in the store and one in the table, the second given the first's account; the server's other tables by user id, the quota's among them, follow the same rule.

**Nothing for FRUS-Explorer.** The analyzer's lot walk copies the rest of the passage at each lot (`String(text[cursor...])`, and twice more for the distance), quadratic in principle; at the server's bounds it reads 20,000 characters of lots in 70 ms, so it is no finding for the kit. The kit's Zotero retry waits are another session's pull request, and were left.

## Session 21f, second follow-up: step 5 holds each mounted file to the export's record of it, and parses only a volume whose file is another

22 November 2026 · branch `claude/optimistic-cray-c16081`, a follow-up session of the phase-3 orchestrator's · [#158](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/158), with S16c's follow-up · upstream `08e8bac8` (tag `1.0-release`), unchanged

S21f's second web follow-up, with no PLAN row of its own: steps 2 to 4 of `docs/prep/upstream-volume-blob-sha.md`, the hand-over of [FRUS-Explorer#1909](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/issues/1909). [#1948](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1948) (`9e582653`) gave index version 75 a record of the file each volume was indexed from, and S12d's pin move to `1.0-release` brought it to the server, its step 1. It is the first of the two upstream changes PLAN's paragraph on S21f named; S21f's follow-up used the second. No file of the app changed, no migration was added and the pin did not move.

**What changed** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/TEIChanges.swift`):
- **The file first.** A volume at a time, once its file's stamp is taken, the job hashes the mounted file with the kit's `VolumeUpdateChecker.gitBlobSHA1(for:)`, the corrections check's git blob SHA-1 of the file's bytes. It holds the hash and the file's length to the export's record of the file the volume was indexed from, which the job reads once through the kit's immutable read-only open of the served export (`IndexingPipeline.indexedVolumeFiles()`). A volume whose file is that file is compared, with nothing parsed and nothing written.
- **Otherwise as before.** A volume whose file is another, or of which the export records none, takes S21f's follow-up's path: its documents hashed with the kit's revision hashes and compared with the export's rows, and the kit's indexer over a volume that differs. The log names each volume whose file is not the one the export indexed, and says once a job how many of its volumes the export records no file for.
- **No record:** a volume indexed before index version 75 has NULL in both columns, and an export from before 75 has neither column, which the kit's read-only open answers with no record. A record that cannot be read counts as none, and the log says why.
- **Unchanged:** the queue, giving way after each volume and going on (`work.json`), the re-check by inode, length and modification time, the record, the comparison index and its placing, and the review's readers. A re-check of a file changed and then put back as the export indexed it passes the volume over, once the volume is taken out of the comparison index as before.
- A test hook, `volumeParsedTestHook`, is told each volume whose documents are compared.

**What follows from it:**
- **An unchanged export** costs a read of each file, where it cost a parse of each volume.
- **An export with a Mac's update history**, S21f's follow-up's "Found, for later": a volume whose mounted file is the one the Mac indexed is now passed over, so a document the Mac's own update removed is no longer indexed and reported again at each first comparison; the served export's own stamp shows that change, as before. A volume whose file is another still meets the seed's rows as that entry describes.
- **An id given twice** in a file the export indexed is passed over too, where the kit stamped it changed at every comparison; the export's own stamp of it, from the Mac's indexing, is the one the reader shows.
- **The synthetic export** records no file (`scripts/synthetic-export` and `SyntheticExport.swift` leave the two columns NULL), so the smoke test's Import server compares its mounted volumes by their documents, as before: CI runs the path an export without the record takes.

**How the done-when is shown,** in `TEIComparisonTests`, where S21f's follow-up left 13 tests:
- **Unchanged:** `anUnchangedExportIsComparedWithNoVolumeIndexed` now parses no volume.
- **Changed:** `aChangedVolumeAloneIsIndexedAndTheKitSaysHowItChanged` parses only the volume whose file changed.
- **The record decides alone** (`theFileTheExportIndexedDecidesWhetherAVolumesDocumentsAreCompared`, new). The export's record of frus1894Nicaragua is the mounted file's blob SHA-1 and length, by the server's hash, and its volume is passed over though its rows say otherwise. A record naming another file has frus1961-63v06's documents compared, found as the export records them, and nothing indexed.
- **No record** (`anExportWithoutTheRecordComparesEveryVolumeByItsDocuments`, new, two cases): with the record NULL, and with its two columns dropped, every volume is parsed and compared as before.
- **The selection's tests:** the rows of a document the TEI does not give, a document with no row or a vanished one, one hashed otherwise, an id given twice and what the selection passes over now give their export no record, as a volume indexed before 75 has none, so they still run the revision-hash comparison.

## Session 21f, follow-up: step 5 compares the kit's revision hashes, and indexes only the volumes that differ

14 November 2026 · branch `claude/clever-gould-1e6506`, a follow-up session of the phase-3 orchestrator's · [#145](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/145) · upstream `b124a59b`, unchanged

S21f's web follow-up, which [FRUS-Explorer#1904](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1904) unblocked, with no PLAN row of its own. PLAN's sentence on #1904 says it: S21f's follow-up "compares the revision hashes with no scratch index, running one only over the volumes that differ". The branch was cut from `main` at `8707814`, #143's merge. No file of the app changed, no migration was added and the pin did not move.

**What changed** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/TEIChanges.swift`):
- **The hashes.** Each volume of the export whose TEI file is in the folder is parsed as `indexVolume` parses it, with the kit's `FRUSDocumentParser().parseVolumeFull(volumeURL:)`. Every document it gives is hashed with the kit's public functions (`revisionHashes(of:)`):
  - `IndexingPipeline.contentHash(header:dateline:sourceNote:bodyText:)`, over `extractHeader`, `extractDateline`, `extractSourceNote` and `extractBodyText`;
  - `bodyHash(for:)`.
- **The comparison.** The hashes are compared with the export's `document_revisions` rows of the volume (`storedRevisions`, `differences`), by the rules in `kit-access-handover.md`'s plan for this follow-up, a row with the last document of its id, as the indexer's writes keep the last. Four things count as a difference:
  - a row at the indexer's version, `currentDateIndexVersion` (74), of a document the file no longer gives;
  - a document with no row, or with one that records it as vanished;
  - a document whose content or body hash is not its row's, at the indexer's version;
  - an id the file gives to documents that hash differently, which the indexer writes in turn (added after the cold review, below).

  A row another version wrote is compared by neither hash, nor when its document has gone: the plan's rule, from the kit's `contentHash` doc, which a test holds to the kit (below).
- **The kit's indexer only over a volume that differs.** A volume with no difference is compared with nothing written. One that differs takes S21f's path as it was: its rows seeded from the export into the scratch index, `indexVolume`, the kit's stamps read, and the volume kept or deleted. So the kit alone says what changed and how; its change-kind statement, `auxUpsertDocumentRevisions`' CASE, is not restated. The log names each volume given to the indexer, and why.
- **Smaller:** the room check on the data volume runs only before a volume is indexed. A file that does not parse is listed as one whose TEI "could not be read to compare it", and an export whose rows of a volume cannot be read as one whose record "could not be read". A test hook, `volumeIndexedTestHook`, is told each volume given to the indexer, and the log names each, with what selected it.
- **The fold, found by this session's first run:** the comparison index placed after a comparison that indexed no volume read as malformed through the immutable open, so the review's readers could not open it and a re-check could not copy it. Before, only a comparison none of whose volumes had a file in the folder reached this, as an Import server started before its TEI folder is filled (the job review found it).
  - An experiment over a scratch index the kit had only made and packed found the cause. The seeding connection had only read the file before the kit's `VACUUM`, and the log was folded and the journal switched through that connection.
  - Folding through a connection opened after the kit's writer and the seeder are let go gave a sound file in every case tried, S21f's own among them. So `place` now does that.
  - A comparison index placed so before this, which a later re-check would copy and fail over at every start until the next import, is set aside: a re-check checks its copy with `quick_check`, and one that does not read whole has every volume compared afresh.
- **As S21f built it:** the job's place in the queue and its giving way after each volume, `work.json`, the re-check by inode, length and mtime, `stoppedFor`, the record of the served file and the compared files, `tei-changes.db` and `tei-changes.json`, and the review's readers. The scratch index is still made as before, the kit's tables empty for a first comparison and a copy of the last comparison index for a re-check, so that the readers, the re-check and the work folder's rule find it where they did; on an unchanged export the kit's indexer never runs in it.

**What follows from the rules:**
- **Results as S21f's.** Over a volume the selection gives it, the kit's stamp is S21f's. Over a volume it passes over, S21f's pass stamped nothing, by the kit's own statements: a row at another version or none is stamped no change, a gone document's included, an unchanged document none, and an inserted row none. `theVolumesTheSelectionSkipsAreOnesTheKitStampsNothingIn` runs the kit's indexer over those rows, as the comparison seeds them, and finds nothing stamped.
- **An id given twice:** the kit writes both documents in turn (`storeIndexData`), and stamps the row changed even on a first index. `frus-parity index` over frus1894Nicaragua with d3's id made d2's stamped d2 `body`, the only one of its 138 rows. So such a volume goes to the kit at every comparison, as it did before, and the kit says d2 changed each time, while the reader opens the first of the two (`anIdGivenTwiceHashedDifferentlySelectsItsVolume`).
- **The synthetic export** holds a few rows of each fixture volume, so each of its mounted volumes still goes to the kit's indexer, as "a document with no row", as every volume did before, and the smoke test's Import server finds nothing changed, as before.
- **An export with a Mac's update history:** S21f's seed writes the export's rows with no change kind, so the kit stamps a gone document's `vanished` row at version 74 vanished again. A volume of an export whose Mac took a correction that removed a document is therefore still indexed, and its document reported, at each first comparison, as before. A `vanished` row of a document the file gives again costs its volume's indexing, with nothing reported. Both are the seed's, below.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- **An unchanged corpus, no scratch index run:** `TEIComparisonTests.anUnchangedExportIsComparedWithNoVolumeIndexed`. Over an export the kit made of the two fixture volumes, both are compared and none is given to the indexer, the hook is never told, and the record and the job's line say nothing changed. The comparison index is in place for the readers, passes `quick_check`, and holds no document or revision row.
- **A changed volume through the scratch index alone, the kit's change kind as now:** `aChangedVolumeAloneIsIndexedAndTheKitSaysHowItChanged` (frus1894Nicaragua corrected, the one volume indexed, d2's `body` change, nothing kept of the other volume). S21f's `UpdateReviewTests` (6) and `TEIComparisonTests` (4) pass unchanged, the review's banner, sheet and tallies among them.
- **Each of the differences selects its volume:**
  - a row at version 74 of a document the TEI does not give: the kit stamps it `vanished` (`aRowOfADocumentTheTEIDoesNotGiveSelectsItsVolume`);
  - a document with no row, and one with a vanished row: both volumes go to the indexer, which records no change of either, and each is deleted from the comparison index again (`aDocumentWithNoRowOrAVanishedOneSelectsItsVolume`);
  - a content hash otherwise: the kit stamps `apparatus` (`aDocumentHashedOtherwiseSelectsItsVolume`);
  - an id given twice, hashed differently: the kit stamps it (`anIdGivenTwiceHashedDifferentlySelectsItsVolume`).

  The rules alone, the version rule, ids given twice and the order of each list among them, are `theSelectionsRules`. What the selection passes over is held to the kit: rows at an older version and at none, of a gone document and of one hashed otherwise, go to no indexer, and the kit's indexer over them stamps nothing (`theVolumesTheSelectionSkipsAreOnesTheKitStampsNothingIn`). A comparison index that does not read whole is compared afresh at the next re-check (`aComparisonIndexThatDoesNotReadWholeIsComparedAfresh`). `TEIComparisonTests` has 13 tests, S21f's 4 among them.
- **The hashes are the kit's stamps:** `UpdateReviewParityTests.theComparisonHashesEachDocumentAsTheKitStampsIt`. Over every document of the four fixture volumes, fixtures/tei's three and own-text's, the comparison's hashes equal the rows the kit's `indexVolume` stamps. Over the synthetic export's rows, which the test before it holds to the kit, they equal the rows. `theRulesAreTheKits` holds the parse and the two hashes in `TEIChanges.swift`, with the two lines it held.
- **Measured in the release image** (below).

|---|---|---|---|
| The fixtures' synthetic export, `fixtures/tei` mounted (2 of its 3 volumes) | 2, their rows partial | 1.05 s, where S21f's took 0.79 | 91 MiB |
| `fixtures/sample`'s 24 volumes (165 MB, 13,687 documents), unchanged | 0 | **11.68 s**, where S21f's took 24.98 | 76 MiB |
| The same, frus1961-63v10's first document changed by one word | 1, its `d1` hashed otherwise; the kit took 1.3 s over it | **12.84 s** | 123 MiB |

- **Each comparison index placed** passed `quick_check`. The unchanged run's held 340 KB, the kit's tables empty; the changed run's held 5.9 MB, the changed volume kept.
