## Session 21f: the corrections check and the update review

13 November 2026 · branch `claude/compassionate-shaw-939180` · [#133](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/133) · upstream `4c252c33`, unchanged

Phase 3's round 6 on the server track, the S21 group's fourth row on the web, after S21e, beside S24e's pin move, on PLAN's defaults, one choice agreed with the orchestrator and one the owner made (below). A Standalone server checks its downloaded volumes for corrections, by the kit's rule, and Update downloads a corrected volume and indexes it again with the kit's `indexVolume`, whose stamp records what the correction changed; an Import server compares its export with its TEI folder, the hash comparison of import step 5 that S2 deferred; and each user reviews what changed in a document they annotated, as the app's banner and review sheet show it, the sheet the web's own over the kit's rules. SPEC's new section, Operating modes ▸ The corrections check and the update review, is the whole account; this entry says what was built where, the decisions, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21g takes from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `38df295`, #131's merge, and the work was kept in local commits until the push; no file of the app changed, no migration was added, and the pin did not move. S24e's pin move to `39859a51` (#132) merged into `main` meanwhile, which the branch does not take (rule 2); the kit files this row compiles are the same at both pins, and CI runs the merge.

**The corrections check and Update** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/Library.swift`, `LibraryIndexing.swift`, `IndexStamps.swift`, `Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminLibrary.swift`):
- Check for Corrections, `POST /api/v1/admin/library/corrections`: GitHub's listing, asked on each press with its ETag (`liveDiff(fresh:)`), and the kit's `VolumeUpdateChecker.updatableVolumes(known:liveInfoByVolumeId:downloadManager:)` over the library, which S21c made the kit's `DownloadedVolumeFiles`. It changes nothing.
- Update is Download: S21c's `VOLUME_INDEXED` refusal of Download for an indexed volume is lifted, since a corrected file is now indexed again. Before a download's file takes its name, the library tells the indexer (`whenFileWillBeReplaced`), which keeps the volume in the stamps as owed a pass (`reindex`, an optional field, so a stamps file of S21d's or S21e's reads), and every request's list takes the owed volumes beside the kit's waiting ones, by the same rules (`volumes(for:writer:)`), so that `indexVolume` runs over a volume the index holds whole, and its `.stamp` records the change. A pass that indexes it, an upgrade's or a reset's included, and its removal, clear it; a start's job takes what a stop left owed (`resumeAtStart`).

**Import mode's step 5** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/TEIChanges.swift`): the kit's `contentHash` and `bodyHash` are internal to its indexer, so the server runs the indexer. `TEIChangeCheck` queues a job, `teiComparison`, after each import and when a start finds an index; the import watcher's loop asks it at each look in `/data/import`.
- The job indexes each volume of the export with `indexVolume` into a scratch index of its own in `/data/tei-check/.work/`, whose revision rows are first the export's with no change, so that the kit stamps what the TEI moved.
- A volume nothing moved in is deleted again as soon as it is compared, its tables with the kit's `removeVolume` and its revision rows, which the kit keeps. One something moved in keeps its tables, for the quotations' check.
- After each volume the job writes its progress, `work.json`, and gives way to any job queued behind it. A job of its own goes on from where it stopped, and a start after a stop goes on with what the stop left.
- Once every volume is compared, the scratch index's log is folded and its journal made a rollback journal's. The record, `tei-changes.json`, is written first and the scratch index then renamed into place as `tei-changes.db`, so that a stop between them leaves the work to place again. The record names the served file, by device, inode, length and the export's stamp, and each volume's TEI file as compared, by inode, length and modification time. The comparison index is read through the kit's immutable open.
- The folder's sweep, the copy for a re-check and each volume's progress run off the actor, which every reader of the comparison waits for.
- Each later look compares the record's files with the folder's. A job compares again, over a copy of the comparison index, only the volumes whose file changed, appeared or went.
- A cancel or an error holds the comparison until the next start, or the next index an import serves, so that a failing one is not queued again at every look.

**The review** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/Reviews.swift`, `Sources/FRUSLightCore/UserReviews.swift`, `ReviewStamps.swift`, `UserHighlights.swift`):
- Each user's review is their row of `annotation_reviews`, which migration 2 made, under the app's derived id, written once (`recordDocumentReview`, on both stores); a change counts as reviewed for a user while their ledger holds its content hash and change kind, the kit's `applyAnnotationReviews` match (`AnnotationReviewLedger.reviews`), so one user's review hides a change from no other.
- A Standalone server records the reviews in the index's `reviewed_at` too, a job of its one writer, `indexReviews`, that applies with the kit's `applyAnnotationReviews` each change every user whose research is on the document has reviewed (`settledReviews`).
- The routes: the banner (`GET …/change`), the sheet (`GET …/review`), Mark Reviewed (`POST …/review` with the content hash and change kind the sheet showed, refused as `DOCUMENT_CHANGED` when another update has stamped another since), and a highlight's Confirm and Move Here (`POST /api/v1/me/highlights/{id}/confirm`, `…/move`), which search again with the kit's `HighlightReanchor.locate` over the page as it renders now and move only to its `.moved` match; `anchorHighlight` on both stores.
- The sentences: the banner's truth table and the sheet's `statusLine`, `searchLine` and `noteRowTitle`, app code, mirrored as `DocumentChangeWords`; the quotations' lines the kit's `ExcerptReview`.

**Research and Administration** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/Research.swift`, `Reviews.swift`'s `AdminUpdateRoutes`): Changed by an update lists the annotated documents with a change the user has not reviewed, `updated` its count, and a row of any list says the change in the kit's words (`changeLine(for:)`) and offers Review Changes…, a removed document's row opening the review (`rowDestination`); `UPDATE_REVIEW_NOT_OFFERED` is gone. `GET /api/v1/admin/library/updates` gives the kit's `VolumeUpdateReview` tallies over the changes that wait for review and every user's research, with Import mode's comparison. A change counts as reviewed by one rule in both modes: once the index holds its review stamp, or once every user whose research is on the document has reviewed it by their ledger, or anyone has where no one's research is. A Standalone server's stamp records the same rule, and an Import server's index can hold only the Mac's.

**The browser app** (`web/src/reader/ReviewSheet.tsx`, `web/src/admin/UpdatesSection.tsx`, `web/src/api/reviews.ts`, `ResearchScreen.tsx`, `LibraryPane.tsx`, `ReaderScreen.tsx`, `copy.ts`'s `review` block and lines beside the research page's and the library's): the banner above the reader's document with Review…; the review sheet, a dialog: What Changed with Mark Reviewed, Highlights with Move Here, Confirm and Remove…, the found words in their surroundings, Quotations, Other Annotations with the notes opened in the note editor and Edit Tags…; Research's Changed by an update and each row's line and Review Changes…; Administration ▸ Library's Keeping Current (Check for Corrections, Update, Update All) and After an Update.

**The decisions:**
- **Where a review is recorded,** put to the orchestrator on 13 November, since SPEC says nothing of an Import server's Mark Reviewed, whose index the server never writes (rule 7), and the index's `reviewed_at` is one stamp for every user of a server: each user's review is their row of the ledger, in both modes, read by the kit's `applyAnnotationReviews` match, so that one user's review hides a change from no other; a Standalone server records it in its index too, as PLAN says, through its one writer, once every user whose research is on the document has reviewed the change; an Import server writes the ledger alone. The orchestrator agreed on 13 November ("Each user's highlights, notes and excerpts are their own, so one user's review must never hide a change from another"), on two conditions, below.
- **Administration's tallies mean the same in both modes,** the first condition: reviewed is the index's stamp or, where it holds none, the ledgers of everyone concerned, computed the same way on both servers, and SPEC says so.
  - The orchestrator offered "reviewed by any user" as one meaning. This row takes everyone concerned instead, since it is the rule the Standalone index stamps by, and a change one user reviewed while another's research still waits on it is one the tallies should still count.
  - The stamp counts as the kit counts it: `VolumeUpdateReview.summaries` passes over a stamped row, and `DocumentRevision` has no public initialiser for a copy without it. So the one difference that follows stays, and SPEC says it: a change the ledgers settled counts again on an Import server when someone new annotates the document, where a Standalone server's stamp keeps it out. The third review found it; a first fix that set the server's own stamps aside fell to the kit's rule, the tests showing it.
  - A disabled account, which can review nothing, is concerned in no review; its research still counts among the annotated documents.
- **The index's stamp waits for everyone concerned,** where the first draft stamped a change once anyone had reviewed it: the kit keeps a document's `body` change marked `body` through a later correction of its notes alone only while the row is unreviewed (its R-5 P3 escalation), so one user's stamped review would have told another, who had not reviewed the text's change, that the text did not change (the server review's fourth point). A user who reviews a change that is no longer the index's sees the escalated one again, which errs towards a warning.
- **Owed in the stamps, not a request alone.** S21d's hand-over proposed a request whose list is its ids (`.reindex(ids)`); a request is held in memory until its job runs, so a stop between a download and its indexing would leave a corrected file the index was never made from, and no list of the kit's would take it again. The owed set is kept in the stamps file, written before the new file takes its name, and every request takes it, which is the same request made durable.
- **Import mode's step 5, a job of the queue after each import, the owner's choice of 13 November.** The orchestrator's second condition: bound the pass by S21a's blob rule if the export or the import records the file each volume was indexed from, and otherwise measure it and ask before building it. Nothing records the file: the export's schema has no per-volume file record, the Mac computes a blob SHA on demand and keeps it in its preferences, and an Import server keeps none. Measured in the release image on the owner's Mac (Docker Desktop, 10 CPUs, one of them busy), the comparison took 0.79 s over the fixtures' two volumes (2.9 MB) and 25.0 s over `fixtures/sample`'s 24 (165 MB, 13,687 documents). The kit's whole pass over the same 24 took 24.7 s. At that rate the 553 volumes would take 8 to 10 minutes there, perhaps 20 to 30 on a small host, with about 100 MiB of memory and a scratch index of tens of MB. The orchestrator put it to the owner, recommending a job that gives way to any queued job after each volume and goes on from where it stopped, with the re-check bounded by each compared file's device, inode, length and modification time. This row leaves the device out of the file's stamp, by the third review's point: a share of a Mac's folder under Docker Desktop can be numbered anew at each start, which would compare every volume again. The owner answered "automatic after each import". The first draft had run the comparison beside the queue so as to hold no job behind it; giving way after each volume does that inside the queue, where Administration's Jobs list shows it and a cancel stops it.
- **Check for Corrections asks GitHub on each press,** where a download within five minutes of the last reading uses it: a check is asked for to see what changed, and with the ETag a listing that has not changed costs nothing with a token.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- The smoke test serves a fixture volume with one document's text changed, finds the change, re-indexes, lists the document under Changed by an update, and reviews a highlight by keyboard on Chromium with no axe violations: its library step's new part, which passed. Check for Corrections found the corrected volume and Update downloaded it. The library's indexing indexed it again with `indexVolume`. Changed by an update listed d2 with the banner's sentence. The spec's `after` phase reviewed the highlight by keyboard with no axe violations (`web/e2e/update-review.spec.ts`), and the `indexReviews` job recorded the review.
- The re-anchor's matches are the kit's, in tests: `UpdateReviewTests.aCorrectedVolumeIsFoundIndexedAgainAndItsChangeReviewed`, where the sheet's match and Move Here's offsets are `HighlightReanchor.locate`'s over the page as it renders after the update, two characters on; and the smoke test's spec, whose moved highlight starts where the page's own offset engine finds the passage.

**Also shown:** a corrected file a stop left before its pass is indexed again at the next start (`aCorrectedFileAStopLeftIsIndexedAgainAtTheNextStart`); Import mode's comparison, a job of the queue, the banner, the sheet and Mark Reviewed over an export, and the tallies waiting for a second user's review, the served file never written (`importModesComparisonWithTheTEIFindsTheChangedDocument`); the comparison giving way to a job queued behind it after a volume and going on from the next, a file changed since compared again alone over the comparison before, a cancel held until a start that goes on with what it left, and a cancel during a volume held though a job is queued (`TEIComparisonTests`); the tallies counting a change again on an Import server when someone new annotates it, and passing over a disabled account (`importModesComparisonWithTheTEIFindsTheChangedDocument`); an export's change its reader reviewed on the Mac left out of the tallies and shown to each user of the server, who reviews it for themselves (`anExportsReviewedChangeIsLeftOutOfTheTalliesAndShownToEachUser`); the ledger on both stores, once under the app's id, each user's own, and the anchor's write (`UserReviewTests`); the ledger's match held to the kit's `applyAnnotationReviews` by running it, the banner's and the sheet's sentences and the copy's words held to the app's source, and the rules called the kit's (`UpdateReviewParityTests`); another user's change still waiting after the owner's review; the two admin routes refused to a reader (`AdminRouteTests`); in the browser app, `ReviewSheet.test.tsx`, `Updates.test.tsx` and the Research test's new cases.

**Two cold reviews,** subagents given the diff and the points the row asks a review to weigh, and none of this session's reasoning: one of the server and its tests, one of the browser app, the smoke test and the spec. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **A check cancelled for another index's could destroy the next one's** (server): every check built in one folder, and a cancelled one went on to its next step, deleting or placing what the next built. Each check now builds in a folder of its own, numbered, and what it does to the status or the files it does only while it is the latest.
- **A reset lost a pending Update's change** (server): its emptying forgot the owed volumes, and its pass rebaselined their new files. A reset of the same file now keeps them owed, and indexes them with `indexVolume` before its pass, with a writer of its own, whose events are not the pass's.
- **Mark Reviewed recorded whatever change was stamped at the press** (server): it now takes the content hash and change kind the sheet showed, as the app's sheet records the revision it loaded.
- **The index's stamp of one user's review changed what another was told** (server): above.
- **The comparison's identity was the file's device and inode alone,** which a later file can reuse after a reset (server): it adds the file's length and the export's stamp, and a check with no index served stops and forgets.
- Smaller, all fixed (server): the comparison's rows read only for a volume it found changed; the fold of its log and its journal's mode checked; room on the data volume checked before each volume; a file not put in place when the stamps cannot record that it is owed a pass; Mark Reviewed answering a job's hold with its 503, not "nothing to review".
- **The main browser suite** (browser): `research.spec.ts` asserted the line S19b gave Changed by an update; the category is shown now only while a change waits.
- **Focus** (browser): after Remove…, focus waited for the row the review's next reading took away; after Update and Update All, for the row that left the list. Each goes on once the reading has come, to the section's heading or to Check for Corrections.
- **Freshness** (browser): the sheet and Research were not read again after the note editor or the tag picker opened from it; they are now, with focus back where the user was.
- **The Research list** (browser): its loading and failure states dropped an open sheet, and a sheet stayed over another category's list; and Edit Tags… failed silently when the tags could not be read. After an Update's tallies are read with the Library's two-second reading while it downloads or indexes. The banner's region is named "A change to this document", since it shows for any change, as the app's does.
- Found by this session's own runs before the reviews: the synthetic export's revision rows held zeros, so an Import server's comparison over the fixtures flagged every document it holds as changed, which would have put a banner over the main browser suite's documents: the export now records the kit's hashes of the fixtures it holds (`Fixtures/export-revisions.sql`, held to the kit by `UpdateReviewParityTests`); the comparison wrote into the served index's folder, which `ServedAPIParityTests` holds to `frus.db` alone, and has a folder of its own; S21c's test expected the refusal this row lifts; the smoke step's note lacked its `runs`; the spec named the category as its text reads, not as its accessible name joins it; and Research's sheet lived in its row, which Mark Reviewed could take away.

**A third cold review,** a subagent given the conditions' diff, `a144cdf..HEAD`, and the requirements, and none of this session's reasoning. It found no defect that records a wrong result or writes the served index, and these, all fixed before the runs:
- **An admin's cancel was dropped when the comparison gave way** (medium): the job gave way after a volume before it looked for a cancel, so a cancel asked during a volume while a user's job was queued ended the job "Finished", and the next went on. It now checks for a cancel first.
- **Blocking work on the actor every reader waits for:** the sweep of the folder every two seconds, and the copy of the comparison index for a re-check, now run off it, as each volume's progress does.
- **A job every look** if a work folder held its progress but no scratch index and could not be removed: a job is queued only for a work folder that holds both.
- **A stop between placing the comparison index and its record** restarted a whole first comparison: the record is written first, and a stop between them leaves the work to place again.
- **The device in the file's stamp,** which a share can number anew at each start (above).
- **Disabled accounts** held a change in the tallies, and from a Standalone index's stamp, for good (above).
- Smaller: the waiting flag after a cancel of the next job raced its submission; a cancelled task now holds the comparison as an error does; `comparison()` reads the record after the index; SPEC's line on a seeded Standalone index's stamps, the two modes' one difference, the footer's sentence for a document no one annotated, and INSTALL's line on a cancel.

It is labelled `Mac`, its body asks for Mac verification and lists Mac check 24, and it is not merged. Under rule 4 it changes shared files, and this repository changes only its records.

**NaturalLanguage, behind `canImport`:** `WordCloudTokenizer`'s counting, `WordCloudMultiLensTokenizer` and `NaturalLanguageReadiness`'s warm-up, gate and engine, with `os`. Where the framework is missing, each declaration that tags is `@available(*, unavailable, message:)`, so the kit tokenises no other way and a host is told why at compile time: `accumulate(from:into:)`'s message reads "WordCloudTokenizer counts with NaturalLanguage, which this platform does not have, and a count made another way would not compare with the bundled clouds or the keyness references: refuse a live count, and read the bundled clouds". The tokenizer's configuration and its filters, `accepts(_:)` and `singularize(_:)`, read no tagger and stay on every platform (a cold review's finding: the app's settings bench asks `accepts` which of a bundled list's words a reader's settings keep). `NaturalLanguageHealth` stays too, its `works(_:)` guarded.

**CryptoKit, and the dependency:** `WordCloudPayloadDigest` imports CryptoKit, or swift-crypto's `Crypto` where CryptoKit is missing, as FRUSCoreKit and SemanticVectorsKit do. Upstream's `Package.swift` declares no package dependency, now as before, and changes in comments only: on Linux this repository's package supplies `Crypto`, for Linux alone, as it does for those two kits. So the app's builds and `swift test` resolve and compile what they did: "No external dependencies found" and no `Package.resolved`, before `swift test` and after, at `v2` and at the head.

**Loading by URL:** `CloudVectorsFile(contentsOf:)` and `KeynessBaselineFile(contentsOf:)` decode the two cloud files and the two references at a URL with a plain `JSONDecoder`, as the app's `BundledCloudVectors` and `BundledKeynessBaseline` do; the two `@MainActor` stores stay the app's, reading `Bundle.main`, unchanged, as S24b's stores did.

**Into the kit:** `Keyness.swift` (`KeynessScore`, `Keyness`) by `git mv` from `FRUSExplorer/Analytics/`, public; `KeynessCloudMeasure`'s two cases (`WordCloudKit/KeynessCloudMeasure.swift`), its label staying the app's in `KeynessCloud.swift`, as `WordCloudLens`'s labels stay in `WordCloudLens+UI.swift`, since the kit has no `String(localized:)` on Linux; the tuning's reading of a reader's settings, out of `WordCloudSettings`' getters into `WordCloudTuning` (`minimumLength(fromSetting:)`, at least 2, 3 when nothing is stored; `minimumCount(fromSetting:)`, at least 1; `foldPlurals(fromSetting:)` and `filterMarkings(fromSetting:)`, on when nothing is stored; and `init(settingsMinimumLength:minimumCount:foldPlurals:filterMarkings:)`, which takes the synced preferences' four values). The getters call them with what they read, and their two defaults are the shipped tuning's.

**`BundledKeynessBaseline`, not moved:** this phase's host refuses the Distinctive measure, live scopes and collocates until its own lemmatiser (phase 4), so it loads no reference and refuses no mismatch. When a host ranks, it has `KeynessBaselineFile(contentsOf:)`, `Configuration.mismatches(against:includeDiplomatic:lexiconsDigest:stopwordsDigest:)` and `WordCloudPayloadDigest`; the rule that picks the reference (the form by the verdict, the tagger's check before the settings') and `KeynessCloud.rank` move then, with `KeynessCloudTests` and `BundledKeynessBaselineTests`, which stay with their subjects.

**The suites:** `KeynessTests` (8) moved with `Keyness` into `WordCloudKitTests/`, opening with `#if SWIFT_PACKAGE`; `project.yml` compiles it into the app's test target too, so the iOS run keeps it. Apple-only, behind `canImport(NaturalLanguage)`, the taggers' suites: `WordCloudMultiLensParityTests`, `WordCloudPrintedFormParityTests`, `UnansweredLemmaRequestTests`, `NaturalLanguageSessionRecordTests`, the readiness engine's lifecycle and the readiness suite's warm-up, canary, `works(_:)` and asset-runtime tests. Wherever the kit builds: the lens rules (4), the adoption rule (`improvesOn`, 6 cases), the word form a verdict gives (3), and the new `WordCloudKitHostTests.swift` (14: the files loaded by URL and held to what the app's reader relies on, the digest held to the references' recorded ones, the tokenizer's filters with no tagger, the tuning from a reader's settings, the measures). `WordCloudKitTests` runs 30 tests in 9 suites on Linux, and lists 90 tests in 13 suites on the Mac where `v2` lists 68.

**Two cold reviews,** given the diff and none of this session's conclusions, one on Apple behaviour and one on the kit, Linux and the suites, during the `v2` baseline. Out of `PersonCoMentionGraphView.swift`, a SwiftUI file, the graphs' label rules the network reads, `GraphLabelRequest` and `GraphNodeLabels`, into `FRUSCoreKit/Analytics/GraphNodeLabels.swift`, unchanged but for access and the `Sendable` the request had by inference; `drawPlate(_:in:)`, which draws into SwiftUI's `GraphicsContext`, stays there.

**What a host supplies:**
- **The label tables:** the kit's `ArchivalCollectionsData.make(authority:usage:coverage:external:labels:subjectNumericLabels:)` takes the external-citation index and the decimal-class table the moved function defaulted to the app's stores, and the subject-numeric table it read from the app's store, as values. The app's `make(authority:usage:coverage:external:labels:)`, with its two defaults, is in `ArchivalCollectionsData+App.swift`, and calls a non-public form that reads the subject-numeric store at each class row's and leaf's reading, where the moved code read it, so no call in the app reads a store at another time. `DecimalClassLabelTable` is public with `init(contentsOf:)`, as `SubjectNumericLabelTable` has been since S22a.
- **The caption measure:** `ArchivalNetworkBuilder.layout(_:in:captionSize:)` takes it. The app's `measuredCaptionSize(_:)`, UIKit's or AppKit's system font at 9 pt semibold, and the `layout(_:in:)` that passes it, as the default did, are in `ArchivalNetworkBuilder+App.swift`.
- **What else it needs, public:** `CollectionAuthorityIndex.collections` and `record(id:)`, and the memberwise initialisers of `ArchivalNetworkGraph`, which "Show only this group" narrows a graph with, and `GraphLabelRequest`, spelt out.

**CoreGraphics behind `canImport`:** the layout and the label rules are geometry. On Apple platforms `CGRect`'s `Equatable`, `.zero` and `union` are CoreGraphics' overlay, which `import Foundation` alone does not bring into the package's module: the package build failed without it. On Linux swift-corelibs-foundation declares the same types with every member the layout calls, checked in this repository's container before the move. So the two kit files import CoreGraphics behind `canImport(CoreGraphics)`, and `FRUSCoreKitBoundaryTests` permits it there, as it does TEIHeaderKit and FoundationNetworking.

**The suites,** by `git mv` into `FRUSExplorerTests/FRUSCoreKit/`, every suite whose subject moved, what needs the app inside `#if !SWIFT_PACKAGE` (tests in Xcode; in the package): `ArchivalAnalyticsTests` (53; 51), `ArchivalNetworkTests` (63; 52), `ArchivalFlowsTests` (18; 18), `ArchivalLibraryProfileTests` (14; 11) and `ArchivalAnalyticsExportTests` (43; 10): 142 of their 191 tests in the package. What stays Xcode's: the views' code, scanned; the composition chart, drawn; the About These Figures popover; the canvas's caption font against the app's measure; the hosted dock and card; and the label counts pinned where UIKit measures the captions. `ArchivalTestSupport.swift` gives the package the app's `make` over the stand-in stores and `layout(_:in:)` with an estimate of the caption font, the measure the network's suites inject there. New: `ArchivalAnalyticsHostTests` (6), the kit's own forms as a host drives them. `GraphNodeLabelTests` (14) and three of `DecimalClassLabelTests`' shipped-corpus rankings join the package. On Linux, `CGRect.intersects` is `true` for two rects that only share an edge (`false` on macOS), so `GraphNodeLabelTests`' plate check compares open intervals itself; no kit code calls `intersects`. The app's scans follow the moved copy (`ArchivalCopyRulesTests`' sources, `ProvenanceStatementTests`' key, ten CountCopy baseline entries), and 43 EditableContent blocks are re-pointed with the amendment log's entry. `FRUSCoreKitTests` goes from 2,335 tests in 294 suites to 2,500 in 307.

**Two cold reviews,** given the diff and none of this session's conclusions, one on Apple behaviour, during the `v2` baseline, and one on the kit, Linux, the suites and a host. Neither found a behavioural change in the app. The fixes: `ProvenanceStatementTests`' key, missed; the request's `Sendable`; SourceNoteKit's guarded import in a moved suite; the plate check's open intervals; the public `make` taking the subject-numeric table as a value, where it first took an autoclosure that a host passing a decode inline would have re-evaluated at each row; the two initialisers; the host suite and the decimal table's loader test; the caption sweep built once (about 30 s of the package's run on a Mac); and the notes they found false or missing. Measured in `swift:6.4-noble`'s Foundation and in Node 22 on nine values, both round a half to the even from the shortest decimal (0.625 → 62%, 0.835 → 84%);

**The neighbours' alias fallback: a deviation from the brief, measured.**
- **The brief** was to give S22d's neighbours route the fallback's two values, `aliasLot` and `aliasName`, in the query.
- **Why not:** three of the authority's records have a name longer than the 1,024 bytes the route allows one `aliasName`: 2,154, 2,472 and 2,650 bytes, among them Indexed Central Files (`txt:department of state|indexed central file`, 23 volumes). The widest record's names run to 5,585 bytes, a query of about 7.5 KB, at nginx's default 8 KB request-line buffer, which INSTALL's recipes sit behind. A row resolving to one of them would have opened a neighbours page that the route refused.
- **Instead:** a row's link names the record, `aliasCollection=<id>`, and the route builds the two values with the kit's `CollectionAliasFallback(record:)` from it. `aliasLot` and `aliasName` stay as S22d made them.
- **Mixing:** naming `aliasCollection` with either of the two is `INVALID_PARAMETER`, and an id the authority lacks is `COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND`.

**The browser app** (`CollectionScreen.tsx`, `VolumeSourcesOutline.tsx`, `sourcesRules.ts`, `api/sources.ts`; lines in `copy.ts`'s two blocks, `router.tsx`'s two routes and `app.css`'s Source Explorer block; `useWidth` and `columnPath` exported from `search/Readings.tsx`, another area's file, for the chart):
- **The record**, in the app's order:
  - NARA Catalog, with the FRUS + NARA catalog chip and the NAID line;
  - Related Collections, each row its own record's link, with the shared volumes and the overlap's meter, the overlap said to a screen reader in the app's words;
  - Cited Over Time;
  - Divided at NARA, each series' View told which series it opens;
  - Pointed At, Not Printed;
  - then S22d's sections.
- **Cited Over Time** is drawn as the search timeline draws its chart, the web's chart idiom at the start, with no screen on `main` drawing with Vega-Lite (the brief): one colour, 4 px data ends, a readout of the era under the pointer, the eras' short labels thinned at a phone's width, the kit's reading as the figure's caption, and the table after it, one disclosure away, with the app's columns and full labels.
- **The lists shown whole are in the address** (`all=related|volumes|pointers`), as the app's Browse keeps its `Expansions` for its host (#1363), so Back from a citing volume returns them as the reader left them.
- **Each record is a page of its own,** keyed by its id, though the page's path is the same. A related record opens with each list at its cap, and the heading takes the focus as a new page's does, on the way back too.
- **The outline's rows:**
  - the Archival Neighbors link, named by the app's spoken words in its three states, with its count, quiet for none; it opens the row's neighbours on This volume, naming its record for the fallback;
  - Collection · cited in N volumes, the record's page;
  - a heading's Cited in N volumes, which opens the app's Cross-Volume Provenance sheet as a dialog, Done returning focus to it;
  - the divided lot's line.
  Each link is a 24 px target, so two that stack at a phone's width stay apart.

Phase 3's row S22d, on the features track after S23e, with no upstream pull request, no pin move and no migration, on PLAN's defaults: Source Explorer over the API and in the browser app, the archival neighbours, a collection authority's record, a volume's Sources outline, and check 8. **The kit's calls,** compiled from the submodule, none copied:

- The readers both views call while drawing (FRUS-Explorer#1895): `SourceExplorerPanels` (the Subject-Numeric citation, the filing periods, the scans' caveat, the neighbours' basis, key and empty state), `SourceExplorerProvenance.lotCards` and `lotRecordGroupSource`, `SeriesFactsIndex.facts` and `creatorName`, `DigitizedRangeIndex.match`, `DigitizedScanPresentation`, `NumericalFileIndex.rolls(forFileNumber:)`, `CuratedLotResolutions`, `CuratedLibraryResolutions`, `PresidentialLibraryOutcome`'s words, `NamedFileSeriesRouting`, `ParisPeaceRecords`, `ManuscriptRepositoryGuidance`, `NARACustody.mayQueryCatalog`, the NARA client's keyless addresses (the client is made for them and never searches), `UnprintedPointer.rowText`, `CountrySeriesOutcome`'s words, `IndexingPipeline.classificationMarking(sourceNote:stored:)` and `DocumentHeaderDisplay.numberedRow`; SourceNoteKit's keys and its `PublishedCitationGrammar`.

**The bundled files** (`SourceExplorerFiles.swift`, a line in `ServerResources.swift`): the files Source Explorer reads beyond the four the server read already (the central files, the volume sources and the lot claimants for a collection's Sources & Archives block, and the collection authority for the graph): the presidential-library catalogue, the curated library and lot resolutions, the series facts, the digitized ranges, the roll scans and the chiefs-of-mission register (`pocom-index.json`, which the classifier's addressee rule reads). Each is read by the kit's own loader once, on the first request that needs it, as the app's stores decode on first use, and gives nothing for a file missing or malformed, as the app's store does; nothing is read at start. The first sources request decodes them off the cooperative pool before it holds the served index, so a job never waits on a decode, the library catalogue only for a library citation. Measured in the container, a debug build, alone: all of them together decode in about a quarter of a second and add about 26 MiB (the authority 8, the central files with the volume sources and the claimants 8, the library catalogue 6, the register 1, the rest under 1). Of the fourteen files PLAN's planning counted, the authority was S23e's and the class labels the indexer's; the usage, external-citation and lot-claimant readers the record's missing sections need are internal at the pin, the accession series is read by no surface, and the source provenance is About the Series' (S24h).

**The server** (`SourceExplorer.swift`, `ArchivalNeighbors.swift`, `ArchivalCollection.swift`, `VolumeSources.swift`, new; lines in `Routes.swift` beside Cite's):
- **`GET /api/v1/volumes/{v}/documents/{d}/sources`,** a document the served index holds: the resolution, then the iOS view's sections in its order, each a panel `kind` with its facts and the kit's words: the note and its classification marking, the Provenance panels the parse case names (central files with the 1906–1910 Numerical File's rolls or gap, the filing period or the periods' table, the Paris Peace Conference and the digitized scans; CFPF; lot files with the curated record group, a post's lot, the lot cards, divided or bundled with the series facts, and the curated outcome; NARA collections; CIA; presidential libraries with the curated finding aid and the catalogue's answer or the custody line; named series with the explainer and the routing; foreign archives; previously published sources with the publication the grammar names; unrecognized notes; the Subject-Numeric citation in any of its wordings), the country series or the no-note section with the era's likely series, the neighbours (thirty rows, the count, the basis and the key), the collection and the unprinted pointers. A NARA Catalog panel names the query `load()` would run (`catalogQuery.route`) and the manual search the app offers; nothing calls NARA. `offline` is what check 8 reads.
- **`GET /api/v1/archival-neighbors`,** the app's `ArchivalNeighborsSheet`'s four requests (a document; a Sources row's keys with the authority's alias fallback, anchored on a volume or not; a collection; a class), its scopes (This volume, This subseries where the subseries has another volume, All volumes) through Related Documents' copy of the rule, its default scope per request, and its rows; a scope the picker does not offer is `SCOPE_NOT_OFFERED`, a document the index lacks `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`.

## Session 21e: sideload, remove, compact and the upgrade

12 November 2026 · branch `claude/s21e-sideload-remove-compact-1c6511` · [#127](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/127) · upstream `4c252c33`, unchanged

Phase 3's round 5 on the server track, the S21 group's third row on the web, after S21d, beside S24b upstream, on PLAN's defaults, with S21d's follow-up folded in: a Standalone server's search answers while a job writes its index, the second half of the owner's choice B of 11 November, which closes the line S21d's done-when moved to that follow-up. A Standalone server serves its own index through the kit's live read-only opens; side-loads a volume's TEI file, listed by the catalogue overlay when the catalogue lacks it and cited with the app's sentence; removes an indexed volume through a job; compacts, checks and resets its index; and at a start re-indexes an index behind the kit's date-index version while search answers. SPEC's Operating modes ▸ Standalone mode's indexing (its served-index bullet) and the new Standalone mode's upkeep and side-load are the whole account; this entry says what was built where, the decisions, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21f and S21g take from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `b7e1e27`, #125's merge, and the work was kept in local commits until the push; no file of the app changed and no migration was added.

**The live stack** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/ServedIndex.swift`, `IndexWriting.swift`, `Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexImport.swift`, `ServerState.swift`), S21d's follow-up, through the opens FRUS-Explorer#1897 put in the pin:
- `CorpusIndex.open(_:live:)` opens a Standalone server's index through `FTS5Store.readOnlyURI(for:)`, `?mode=ro` without `immutable`, at the start, after an import that seeds it and after each job; it is marked `isLive`, and `ServedIndex` then opens `FTS5Store(readingLiveDatabaseAt:)`, `IndexingPipeline(readingLiveIndexAt:…)`, with the user store attached as before, and the page-range, person and cross-reference stores' `init(databaseURL:…)`. Import mode keeps every immutable open and its swap: `live` is false by default, the importer's `liveReads` and the start's open follow the mode, and the stack branches on `isLive`.
- A live open's version is its documents' own record, the lowest `document_revisions.index_version` of a document the index holds (`ExportChecks.checkLiveVersions`, the kit's own `EXISTS` in `document_cache`, so that the revisions it keeps of removed volumes count for nothing), refusing an index with a document of a later version; the export's stamp is no longer the version of an index the server has indexed into.
- `ServedIndexWriting` serves the index while the indexing job writes it: after each volume and at the job's end it opens `CorpusIndex` again and serves it, so that the counts, the volumes a working corpus resolves against and the stack's caches follow each volume. A job that holds the index to itself names why (`willWriteIndex(at:holding:)`, `ServerState.indexHold`): a compaction, and a reset while it empties the index; meanwhile search answers 503, `INDEX_BEING_WRITTEN`, in its sentence, and `/readyz` `indexing_library`, as S21d's indexing did. S21d's `indexWriteUnfinished` is gone: a log a reader keeps from folding at a job's end is read through, and folded by the next job or start. The provider lets go of released stacks as it opens new ones.

**The side-load** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminLibrary.swift`, `Sources/FRUSLightCore/Library.swift`, `UserLibrary.swift`, `ServerResources.swift`): `POST /api/v1/admin/library/sideload?file=<name>` in a group of its own, whose guard takes XML (`UserDataGuard.mediaTypes`) of 64 MiB at most, the route refusing past the limit as it streams. The name gives the id by the app's rule, the name less `.xml`, and only a name of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, beginning with a letter or digit, of 128 characters at most and no other volume's figures folder or sidecar (`VolumeLibrary.sideloadedVolumeId(fromFileName:)`). The upload goes to a hidden staging folder, which a start removes; the kit's `SideloadValidator` reads it into a folder of the library's own, where it is flushed, and it takes its name by `link(2)`, which refuses a name taken meanwhile, so that the duplicate check and the placing are one step; the store keeps the row `sideloaded = 1`, with its hash, length and time and no figures (`recordLibrarySideload`, on both stores). A volume the catalogue lacks needs a header the kit's `LocalVolumeCatalog` reads. Its indexing is a job, `.asked`. FoundationXML on Linux resolves no external entity with the kit's parsers' defaults and libxml2 stops an entity that expands without end (error 89), measured in the build image before any code and held by a test and the smoke test, so no gate of the server's own was added before the kit's parsers.

**The catalogue overlay** (`ServerResources`): `LocalVolumeCatalog.reconcile(in:known:)` at each Standalone start and after each side-load and removal, the later of two refreshes kept; `volume(_:)` answers for a side-loaded volume as the app's `ManifestStore.entry(forVolumeId:)` does, so the reader, Browse (listed after the catalogue's, `sideloaded`), the Library (`catalogued`, false) and every route that names a volume take it, and Citation Lookup, Add Documents' citations and the cross-reference store read the published catalogue alone, as the app's `citableEntries` and `bundledEntries` do (#1523). A side-loaded volume's citation, its records and the reader's document carry no history.state.gov link, and the citation carries the app's sentence, the server's (`citation.sideloaded.note`, held to the app's).

**The index's upkeep** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexUpkeep.swift`, new, `Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminIndex.swift`, new, `AdminStatus.swift`), each a job of the indexer's, the index's one writer:
- **Remove** of an indexed volume (`libraryRemove`): the kit's `removeVolume(_:)`, the server's record and the sentinel forgotten, the passes after indexing, the log folded, the index opened again, then `VolumeLibrary.remove(_:)`, which now takes a side-loaded id and its sidecar; the removal kept in the stamps from its first write until its files are gone, finished by the next start; a second removal of a volume refused; one that fails forgotten. The route's `VOLUME_INDEXED` refusal is lifted where an indexer is.
- **Compact** (`indexCompact`): `vacuumIndex()`, holding the index to itself, once the data volume has the room this server's copy needs, twice the live size and 64 MB, checked through a live read-only open before the hold; whether a compaction is worth offering is the app's `IndexCompaction`, mirrored as `IndexCompactionRule` (`IndexUpkeepParityTests`). **Check** (`indexCheck`): `checkIndexIntegrity()` while search answers. `GET /api/v1/admin/index` gives the room.
- **The pass over every volume:** an upgrade and a reset re-index with the kit's `indexAllVolumes()`, as the app's launch and its Rebuild From Scratch do, which rebaselines revisions rather than stamping them, the index served and opened again after each volume as the kit's progress stream says it stored it, a volume that fails kept failed with the stage its pass reached; it runs to its end once begun, as the app's does.
- **Reset, Standalone's** (`indexReset`, `POST /api/v1/admin/index/reset`): `removeAllVolumesFromIndex()` under the hold, the stamps forgotten (`indexWasReplaced(sameFile:)`, the side files kept), then the pass; kept in the stamps until the pass ends, so that a stop's cut is finished at the next start.
- **At a start** (`prepareAtStart`, before the index is opened): the writer's open migrates the schema; full-text tables of an earlier generation are rebuilt from the cache before the index is served (`rebuildSearchIndexFromCache()`); a cut-short reset is emptied again; a cut-short removal's index part is finished, then its files; and when the stamps' date-index version is behind the kit's (`installedDateIndexVersion`, a stamp of 0 reading as the documents' lowest), an upgrade begins, which the start's job, the pass, does while search answers and `/readyz` names the volumes still to go; the stamps are the kit's once the pass has run, whatever failed, as the app marks them. Before an import replaces a Standalone index, its log is folded (`indexWillBeReplaced`).

**The decisions:**
- **The upgrade and the reset run the kit's pass over every volume,** not the indexing job's `indexVolume` a volume at a time, which the first draft used: `indexVolume` stamps a document's change, and a document an earlier parse left out that a later parse emits again would read as changed by an update; `indexAllVolumes()` is how the app re-indexes after a version bump and after its wipe, rebaselining, and the kit has no public single-volume rebaseline. So an upgrade a stop cuts short is begun again by the next start, whose pass takes every volume again, as the app's launch runs its pass again, and the pass takes no cancel once begun, as the app's takes none. A volume the index holds with no file in the library, as a seeding export's can be, is outside the pass and keeps its version until it is downloaded and S21f's Update indexes it.
- **Compaction's room is the server's own,** twice the live size and 64 MB: SQLite's temporary copy is on the data volume (`SQLITE_TMPDIR`), and the copied pages go to the log as well, where the app's 1.15 times the live size, which the pane's words keep, is the margin for its own temporary folder.
- **No gate of the server's own before the kit's parsers:** the kit's parsers' defaults on Linux already resolve no external entity, and libxml2 stops an expansion that runs away, both shown in the image; a gate would refuse files the app takes.

**How the done-when is shown:**
- A side-loaded fixture volume is read and cited with the sentence: `LibraryUpkeepRouteTests.aSideloadedVolumeIsReadAndCitedWithTheAppsSentence` (a copy of frus1894Nicaragua under an id the catalogue lacks: its row, the Library, Browse, the reader, search and its citation with the app's sentence and no link); and the smoke test's library step, in the image.
- A volume removed is gone from search, Browse and the reader: `aRemovedVolumeIsGoneFromSearchBrowseAndTheReader`; the smoke step removes the two it side-loaded.
- The smoke test compacts and checks: its library step, after the removals, the index's file smaller and its check passing; `theIndexIsCompactedAndChecked` in Swift.
- A run killed between volumes is finished at the next start, in a test: `IndexUpgradeTests.anUpgradeAStopCutShortIsFinishedAtTheNextStart`, the first server stopped inside its pass and the next start's pass finishing every volume; `aResetAStopCutShortIsFinishedAtTheNextStart` and `aRemovalAStopCutShortIsFinishedAtTheNextStart` for the other two.
- A volume indexed under a lowered stamp is re-indexed at start: `aVolumeIndexedUnderALoweredStampIsReindexedAtTheStart`, `/readyz` naming the volume still to go while the index is served.
- S21d's moved line, a search during indexing answers: `LibraryIndexingRouteTests.searchAnswersWhileAJobWritesTheIndex`, S21d's test turned around, a search held inside a volume's pass finding its documents while the kit names it unfinished; and the smoke step, whose search answers 200 between two readings of Status naming the indexing job running.

**Also shown:** the side-load's refusals, a name for each rule, the media type, the length and the stream (`theSideloadRefusesWhatIsNoVolume`); its external entity and entity bomb (`aSideloadedFilesExternalEntitiesAreNeverRead`); the library's side-load whole or not at all and the store's row on both stores (`SideloadTests`); full-text tables of an earlier generation rebuilt at the start; Standalone's reset (`aStandaloneResetEmptiesTheIndexAndIndexesTheLibraryAgain`); a second removal refused; the compaction's rule and the citation's sentence held to the app's source (`IndexUpkeepParityTests`); and the new routes refused to a reader (`AdminRouteTests`). In the browser app, `web/src/admin/Upkeep.test.tsx`.

**Two cold reviews,** subagents given the diff and the points the row asks a review to weigh, and none of this session's reasoning: one of the server and its tests, one of the browser app, the smoke test and the records. What held up was fixed before the push:
- **The upgrade could never finish, and stamped changes no file made** (server): the first draft re-indexed with `indexVolume`, kept a failed volume pending for good, and stamped a returning document as changed; the upgrade and the reset now run the kit's pass, above.
- **Removed volumes' revisions held the live version down** (server): the version now counts documents the index holds.
- **Two removals of one volume could be queued,** the second wedging it (server): the indexer refuses the second in the step that takes the first, and a failed removal is forgotten.
- **A reset a stop cut short left the full-text tables empty** (server): the reset is kept in the stamps and finished at the next start.
- **Compaction's room was the app's margin** (server): the server's own, and checked before the hold.
- **An import replacing a Standalone index could leave the old log beside the new file's name,** which a live open would read (server): the log is folded before the install.
- **Two overlay refreshes at once could keep the older listing** (server): the later is kept.
- **The browser's caches never followed the index** (browser): the shell reads again what it reads of the index when `/readyz`'s sentence changes, and a side-load and a removal ask again what Browse and search read.
- **Download Again for a volume the catalogue lacks; Index All Waiting counting what the server will not take; buttons marked unavailable that acted; a removal under way not shown** (browser, server): the Library gives `catalogued` and `removing`, the route counts the overlay's volumes, and the pane guards what it marks.
- **The smoke's poller could die at one missed reading, and the compaction's check showed nothing** (smoke): the poller survives, and the compaction must shrink the file.
- **The records** said more than the code: Browse's mark, the compaction's time, the reset's search, the error codes, which the docs now say as the code does.
- Left as they are, each said where it matters: Citation Lookup and the cross-reference store read the published catalogue alone, as the app's do (#1523); and a volume a seeding export holds with no file keeps its version through an upgrade, for S21f.

**The runs before the push,** at `5e73f1b`, each in one hold of `heavy.sh`; after them only the records changed, and the words of one line the smoke test prints:
- CI's swift job, `scripts/swift --postgres test`, this package's own targets built clean: the build in 86 s with no warning; 3,756 tests, CrossRefKitTests 10, FRUSCoreKitTests 2,159, FRUSLightCoreTests 271, FRUSLightServerTests 345, FRUSParityTests 251, FRUSRichTextTests 42, FTS5CheckTests 3, FTS5StoreTests 219, GeneratorKitTests 7, ManifestGeneratorTests 60, SemanticVectorsKitTests 40, SourceExplorerExportGeneratorTests 22 and SourceNoteKitTests 327, this row's 16 among them (`IndexUpgradeTests` 5, `SideloadTests` 3, `LibraryUpkeepRouteTests` 6, `IndexUpkeepParityTests` 2) with S21d's test it turned around, and the one skip the job allows, `backupExclusion()`. Three issues, none this row's: two tests of the user store on PostgreSQL, `UserLeadsTests.leadsAreKeptAsTheAppKeepsThem` and `UserSummaryTests.aSummaryFromAResearchDatabaseMayBeDeletedButNotChanged`, were refused a connection, "sorry, too many clients already", the limit of 100 clients Session 21d's entry describes, and `FRUSLightCoreTests` with PostgreSQL then passed twice running, 271 tests each; and `RelatedDocumentsParityTests.aSeededProjectsLeadsAreTheAggregators` read a Project Home holding the leads of the computation before the one it waited for, 23 where the kit gives 24, the suite then passing twice running alone (Found in passing, below).

The library step's search answered 200 six times while the indexing job wrote the index, each between two readings of Status naming the job running; a volume was side-loaded under an id the catalogue lacks, listed from its header, indexed and cited with the app's sentence and no link, and a file's external entity read nothing of the image's; the two side-loaded volumes were removed, the index compacted from 6 MB to 5 MB and checked; check 2 passed over the Standalone index; and the browser suite passed, 82 tests at the root and 82 under the path, with the library spec's Standalone test on the Standalone server.

**Found and fixed: the runtime image's time zones.** The first smoke run found every graph request trapping the server (SIGTRAP, exit 133) on the Standalone project, which runs, like the rest of the smoke test, under `TZ=America/New_York`, the zone the install guide offers for the backup's hour. Foundation's `DateFormatter` and `DateIntervalFormatter` read a zone from `/usr/share/zoneinfo`, which `ubuntu:24.04` leaves out, and trap without it; UTC needs no file, and the calendar's arithmetic reads ICU's own zones. A probe of each call in the runtime image found it, and `tzdata`, about 1.4 MB, cures it: the runtime stage installs it, with `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`, a package decision of this row's, as libcurl was S21c's, since rule 4 reserves the image's packages to S20a and S20b. ## Session 21d: indexing on the server

11 November 2026 · branch `claude/sad-greider-f4235c` · [#121](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/121) · upstream `68bffcf6`, unchanged; [FRUS-Explorer#1897](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1897), open, awaiting Mac check 25 · records [#122](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer-Web-App/pull/122)

**Since merged** (S23c's pin move records it): the upstream pull request, [FRUS-Explorer#1897](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1897), merged on 11 November (22:24 UTC) as `4c252c33`, whose tree is its head's, `b36e1db0`, onto `v2` at `782127ff`, so Mac check 25 is done. S23c's pin move took it, so the follow-up that serves the index while a job writes it starts at the pin.

Phase 3's round 4 on the server track, the S21 group's second row on the web, after S21c, beside S23d and, upstream, S24a. A Standalone server indexes the volumes its library downloads into its own index, with FRUSCoreKit's read-write pipeline, in jobs of the server's queue, keeps the kit's stamps in a file beside the index, keeps each volume a pass did not index with the stage the kit's stream gave, and stops between volumes when cancelled. SPEC's new section, Operating modes ▸ Standalone mode's indexing, is the whole account; this entry says what was built where, the two decisions, how the done-when is shown, what the reviews changed, and what S21e to S21g take from it. The branch was cut from `main` at `2a0f10a`, #115's merge, after #117, and the work was kept in local commits until the push.

**The kit had no read-only open without `immutable`.** PLAN's row serves a Standalone index "read-only without `immutable`", so that search reads each volume as its store commits. At the pin and at `v2`'s head `9e6cc2af`, `FTS5Store(readingDatabaseAt:)` and `IndexingPipeline(readingIndexAt:…userStore:)` open `?mode=ro&immutable=1` alone; their other opens are read-write, and the user store's attach, which every signed-in search reads (S17d), is the immutable open's alone. `PageRangeStore(databaseURL:)` and `PersonMentionStore(databaseURL:)` already read without it. An immutable reader of a file in write-ahead-log mode reads the main file with no lock and never the log, so it sees a stale index, and torn pages once a checkpoint runs: no web-side way round it is correct. The orchestrator put two orders to the owner, who chose B on 11 November: this row merges with a Standalone server's search refused while a job writes, and a follow-up serves the index while it is written, once a pin move carries the kit's new opens. So **the done-when's "a search during indexing answers" moves to that follow-up, by the owner's choice of 11 November.** The upstream pull request is part of B, and is Mac check 25: FRUS-Explorer's branch `claude/live-read-only-index-opens`, cut from `v2` at `9e6cc2af`, adds `FTS5Store(readingLiveDatabaseAt:schema:)`, with `FTS5Store.readOnlyURI(for:)`, and `IndexingPipeline(readingLiveIndexAt:fts5Store:resources:volumesDirectory:userStore:)`: `?mode=ro` without `immutable`, the user store attached as on the immutable open, the immutable and read-write opens as they were, and nothing the app calls. `IndexReadOnlyOpenTests` shows the live open, beside a writer that keeps the file open, answering as the writer does, seeing a volume indexed after it opened, its documents before its pass finishes, refusing every write and refusing what the immutable open refuses; `SearchUserSourceTests` shows its attach. The kit's suites pass on the Mac over it, `FRUSCoreKitTests` 2,049 tests in 261 suites and `FTS5StoreTests` 219. Its pull request, [FRUS-Explorer#1897](https://github.com/joshbotts/FRUS-Explorer/pull/1897), opened after this one, rebased onto `v2`'s `782127ff` (#1896) before it opened, with the whole check at its head `b36e1db0` beside `v2` there, in one hold: both app builds with `v2`'s warning lines; the iOS unit run on the iPhone 17e, 7,970 tests in 958 suites against 7,966, failing only where `v2` fails, the same 17 tests and 2 suites skipped; `swift test`, 4,118 tests in 492 suites against 4,114, `FRUSCoreKitTests` 2,159 in 276 against 2,155; the Mac symbol diff, 16 names removed and 25 added, all in the initialisers it changes; and Linux over `main` `c227009`, 3,690 tests against `v2` alone's 3,686, with the same 24 issues in the parity suite, line for line, and the access proof compiled. The live test, run with the immutable opens in its place, fails at the open, "schema generation 0": the writer's schema is still in the log. With `v2` alone over the same copy of `main`, `RelatedDocumentsParityTests.aSeededProjectsLeadsAreTheAggregators` fails, value for value as with the branch, beside the 23 issues the pin move settles (21 golden files made from the pin's sources, and 2 reads of the file #1891 moved); S24a saw it pass with `9e6cc2af` over `2a0f10a`, so the next pin move meets it. A records-only pull request, #122, named it here.

**The decision: what queues the indexing.** S21c's hand-over weighed two hooks: an indexing job queued when a download job ends with volumes downloaded, or a job reading `library_volumes` for files whose blob SHA differs from what the index last took. The first is taken: a download job that fetched volumes, however it ends (succeeded, failed in part, cancelled or stopped by a host), queues a job for every volume that waits, by the kit's own list (`volumesAwaitingIndex(excluding:)`), those whose last pass failed left out unless the download fetched them again. The queue runs one job at a time, so the indexing runs once the download has ended, and a job asked for while another waits joins it. The second hook needs what the index last took of a file, which nothing records yet: the corrections check (S21f) compares blob SHAs with the listing's, and its Update downloads and then indexes through this job. Two more queue a job: a start, once the index found there is open, for what waits, less a volume whose pass a stop of the server cut short, which the kit's sentinel names, as the app's launch leaves such a volume to its reader; and an admin's Index.

**The stamps** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/IndexStamps.swift`), `IndexStampFile`, the kit's `IndexingStampStore` over `/data/index/index-stamps.json`: what the app keeps in `UserDefaults` (the date-index and FTS-schema versions, the rollup's version, fingerprint and date-index version, the broken-references index applied, and `IndexingStateTracker`'s sentinel), read back as the kit's `InMemoryIndexingStampStore` reads them, with the server's record of each volume a pass did not index (`IndexingFailureRecord`: failed or stopped, the stage, the sentence, when). Each change writes the file whole under a hidden name, `fsync`s it, renames it over the old and `fsync`s the folder, under one lock, so a restart reads it as it was before a change or after it; a failed write keeps the change in memory and is made again with the next. A file that cannot be read is set aside, and the stamps begin again, which makes the kit's gated passes run again. An import that installs an export in the index's place clears them (`IndexerAfterIndexImport`).

**The job** (`Sources/FRUSLightCore/LibraryIndexing.swift`), `LibraryIndexer`, built at every start and wired in `ServerComponents.make`, `libraryIndex` beside the queue's other kinds:
- It waits for the index a start found to be opened, refuses to write an index the server does not serve (one the start refused), opens the kit's read-write `IndexingPipeline` with the stamps and the tracker, turns on `setStopsBetweenBatchesWhenCancelled(true)`, and takes the kit's list of what waits.
- Each volume is a step: a cancel between volumes stops it there. The pass runs in a task group beside a watcher of the job's cancel, which cancels the pass so that S21a's stop ends it once its documents are stored; the volume is then kept as stopped, `storingTables`, and the next indexing finishes it. A volume is not begun when the data volume would keep less than 64 MB free beyond twice its file.
- The kit's `progressStream` is read as it comes (`IndexingProgressRelay`): its updates say the job's line, reading the XML, then storing the documents and the other tables, and its last stage before `.failed` is kept with a volume that fails, the sentence the server's: the parser's error and where, never a path. A SQLite failure that means the index cannot be written stops the job, the rest not tried.
- Then the passes after indexing, `runPostIndexPasses`, over what was indexed, a cancel's job included, and the date-index and FTS stamps set to this build's after a first pass, as the app sets them, since every index this server serves is at the kit's version.
- The writer is let go at the end, its connections closing, and the job folds the write-ahead log into the file with `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` through a connection of its own, before the served index is told.
- `Library.swift` (S21c's) tells it the volumes each download job fetched (`whenDownloadsEnd`), on every way the job ends.

**The served index while a job writes, B** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/IndexWriting.swift`, `ServedIndex.swift`, `ServerState.swift`): before the job's first write, `ServerState.indexBeingWritten` is set, and the provider lets go of its stack and waits, five minutes at most, until no request holds one, by weak references to the stacks it opened. Meanwhile every route that reads the index answers 503, `INDEX_BEING_WRITTEN`, a plain refusal naming the indexing, `/readyz` answers a new step, `indexing_library`, which the browser app's banner shows, and the reader renders from the volumes' files, as it does with no index (`servedIfReady()` gives none). Once the job has closed the index, it is opened again (`CorpusIndex.open`) and served, `ServerState.indexWritten(_:)`, with the counts it holds now. Import mode is unchanged: the indexer refuses it, and the immutable open and the import's swap are as they were.

**The routes** (`Sources/FRUSLightAPI/AdminLibrary.swift`, S21c's): `GET /api/v1/admin/library` adds `indexing` (`active`, `volume`), a status `indexing`, and for a volume whose file is in place and whose last pass did not index it, `failed`, with `index` (`state`, `stage`, `at`) and `error` the server's sentence; `POST …/library/index`, `{"volumeIds": [...]}` or `{"all": true}`, 202 with the job, refusing a volume not in the library, one indexed whole (`VOLUME_INDEXED`), nothing waiting (`NOTHING_TO_INDEX`) and Import mode; and Remove refused while a job may index the volume (`INDEXING_IN_PROGRESS`). Status gives the job's line through S20d's `jobs.running`, unchanged.

**The browser app** (`web/src/admin/LibraryPane.tsx`, `web/src/api/library.ts`, `copy.ts`'s admin block): the Indexing state, **Index** on each volume that waits, **Index All Waiting**, a line naming the volume a job indexes, Download Again hidden while a pass reads a volume's file, and the Library read again every two seconds while an indexing job waits or runs; the job's kind, Library indexing; `indexing_library` among `api/types.ts`'s readiness steps.
